nodes.title: Linear independence of characters
nodes.statement: Let G be locally profinite and π₁, …, πₙ pairwise non-isomorphic irreducible admissible complex representations. Then Θ_{π₁}, …, Θ_{πₙ} are linearly independent functionals on C_c^∞(G) ([Cas95] Proposition 2.3.1). Consequently an admissible finite-length representation is determined up to semisimplification by its character, and a finite sum Σ n_σ Θ_σ with distinct σ determines the multiplicities n_σ.
hypotheses: G locally profinite; representations irreducible admissible and pairwise non-isomorphic.
proofSteps: Choose a compact open K with every πᵢ^K ≠ 0; each πᵢ^K is a simple H(G, K)-module and they are pairwise non-isomorphic (SR.1 corner-irreducibles).
By the density theorem the map H(G, K) → ∏ᵢ End(πᵢ^K) is onto, so there are fⱼ ∈ H(G, K) with tr πᵢ(fⱼ) = δᵢⱼ ([Cas95] Proposition 2.3.1, citing Jacquet–Langlands Lemma 7.1).
Semisimplification: by Jordan–Hölder and additivity Θ_V = Σ m_σ Θ_σ over the irreducible constituents, and linear independence recovers the m_σ.
acceptance: For GL₂(ℚ_p), the reducible principal series i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) and 1 ⊕ St have the same character, though they are not isomorphic.
The trivial and Steinberg characters of GL₂(ℚ_p) are linearly independent.

sources.match: The distribution characters of finitely many inequivalent irreducible admissible representations are linearly independent (2.3.1); irreducible admissible representations with the same character are isomorphic (2.3.2).

nodes.title: Miličić's theorem on limits of unitary characters
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G. Let (πₙ) be irreducible unitarizable representations whose characters converge weakly. Then there are a finite set S of irreducible unitarizable representations and integers n_σ > 0 with lim Θ_{πₙ}(f) = Σ_{σ∈S} n_σ Θ_σ(f) for all f ∈ C_c^∞(G), and S = L[πₙ] = C[πₙ] in the Fell topology (Gan–Savin Theorem 11.1; Miličić 1973, Theorem 5). In particular, under weak convergence of characters, limit points and cluster points coincide and form a finite set.
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G.
πₙ irreducible unitarizable, with weakly convergent characters.
proofSteps: The C*-algebra of G has bounded trace on the K-fixed parts (uniform admissibility, SR.3a): for every K, dim πₙ^K ≤ c(G, K); this is the hypothesis of Miličić's theorem on C*-algebras with bounded trace.
Fell convergence of irreducible unitary representations of such algebras is controlled by traces: πₙ → σ iff Θ_σ ≤ lim inf of Θ_{πₙ} on positive elements of the K-corners, for every K (Miličić).

With weakly convergent characters the limit functional Θ is positive on positive K-corner elements and has finite rank on each corner (bounded by c(G, K)); it decomposes as a finite sum Σ n_σ Θ_σ by linear independence (characters-linearly-independent), and the σ occurring are exactly the limit and the cluster points.
The analytic part of this argument is cited from Miličić through Gan–Savin and Tadić [Ta1]; its decomposition into C*-algebra lemmas is listed under the layer's remaining refinements.

The passage from bounded ranks on each Hecke corner to one globally finite character decomposition is not a consequence of linear independence alone. It is precisely the bounded-trace C*-algebra theorem recorded in the gap; do not treat the preceding outline as closing that step.
acceptance: For a constant sequence πₙ = σ, S = {σ}, n_σ = 1 and L = C = {[σ]}.
For SL₂(ℚ_p) and complementary series πₙ converging to the endpoint, lim Θ_{πₙ} = Θ_1 + Θ_St, so S = {1, St} = L[πₙ]: the limit set has two points, reflecting that the unitary dual is not Hausdorff.

sources.match: If the characters of irreducible unitarizable πₙ converge weakly, the limit is a finite positive integral combination of characters of unitary representations σ ∈ S, and S equals both the set of limit points and the set of cluster points.

sources.locator: D. Miličić, On C*-algebras with bounded trace, Glasnik Mat. 8 (28) (1973), Theorem 5; M. Tadić, Glasnik Mat. 23 (1988) (not read)
sources.match: The original statement and its p-adic application, as Gan–Savin cite them.

nodes.title: Tadić: compactness of tempered characters and continuity of supports
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G. Let M be a Levi subgroup and (τₙ) irreducible tempered representations of M. Then some subsequence has weakly convergent characters, with limit the character of a (possibly reducible) admissible finite-length representation τ of M; and the cuspidal support of every constituent of the limit is the limit of the cuspidal supports of the τₙ in the Bernstein variety Ω(M) (SR.3) (Gan–Savin §11.1 and §10.3, citing Tadić).
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G.
τₙ irreducible tempered; unitary central characters.
proofSteps: Uniform admissibility bounds dim τₙ^K by c_K. For K-biinvariant f, |Θ_{τₙ}(f)| ≤ c_K‖f‖₁, since the integrated unitary operator has norm at most ‖f‖₁. Second countability gives a countable spanning family of C_c^∞(M); diagonal subsequence extraction produces a weak character limit, possibly zero.

Apply milicic-limits to identify a nonzero limit as a finite positive-integer combination of irreducible unitary characters. The bounded-trace prerequisite of that theorem remains an explicit gap. The support is tempered, since each τₙ is weakly contained in the regular representation and this support is Fell closed.

For a nonzero limit, every constituent is a Fell limit of the subsequence by Miličić; fell-convergence-bernstein-centre gives convergence of the common cuspidal supports to that of every constituent. With zero limit the constituent assertion is vacuous.

This replaces the unsupported assertion that fixed K permits only finitely many inducing discrete-series supports and a fixed summand position. No global finite-length character is deduced solely from local finite-rank limits.
acceptance: For M = T a split torus, the τₙ are unitary characters; the theorem reduces to compactness of the unitary unramified characters together with finiteness of characters of T ∩ K of bounded conductor at fixed level.
Without temperedness the conclusion fails: |·|^{n} on ℚ_p^× has no weakly convergent subsequence of characters.

sources.match: By [Ta1] the tempered parts τₙ° have a subsequence whose characters converge weakly to the character of a not necessarily irreducible τ°.
By [Ta1] the supercuspidal support of a limit is the limit of the supercuspidal supports.

sources.locator: M. Tadić, On limits of characters of irreducible unitary representations, Glasnik Mat. 23 (1988) 15–25 (not read)
sources.match: The cited source.

nodes.title: Fell convergence implies convergence in the Bernstein centre
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G. If irreducible unitarizable πₙ converge in the Fell topology to an irreducible unitarizable π, then their infinitesimal characters (cuspidal supports in the Bernstein variety Ω(G), SR.3 bernstein-centre-blocks) converge to that of π: for every z in the Bernstein centre, z(πₙ) → z(π), and eventually πₙ lies in the Bernstein component of π. Consequently every irreducible constituent of a weak limit of characters of the πₙ has the cuspidal support of π (Gan–Savin §11.1, citing Tadić [Ta2]).
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G.
proofSteps: Fix K with π^K ≠ 0; Fell convergence and K-types (k-types-persist) give πₙ^K ≠ 0 for large n, so the πₙ lie in the finitely many Bernstein components meeting level K (SR.3 finite-type-corners).

On the K-corner, the centre of H(G, K) acts on the simple modules πₙ^K by characters; Fell convergence gives convergence of the matrix coefficients ⟪v, πₙ(f)v⟫ for f in the centre of the corner and smooth vectors approximating a K-fixed vector of π, hence of the central characters (Tadić [Ta2]).
Regular functions on the Bernstein variety are the centre (SR.3 bernstein-centre-blocks), so convergence of all central characters is convergence in Ω(G).
acceptance: For G = ℚ_p^×, Fell convergence of unitary characters χₙ → χ means eventually equal restriction to ℤ_p^× and χₙ(p) → χ(p), which is convergence in the Bernstein variety.

sources.match: Since convergence in the Fell topology implies convergence in the Bernstein centre [Ta2], the constituents of the limit lie in any principal series containing the limit σ.

sources.locator: M. Tadić, Geometry of dual spaces of reductive groups (non-Archimedean case), J. Analyse Math. 51 (1988) 139–181 (not read)
sources.match: The cited source.

nodes.title: K-types persist in limits
nodes.statement: Let G be locally profinite, K a compact open subgroup and τ a smooth irreducible representation of K. If π is irreducible unitarizable, τ occurs in π|_K, and π is a limit point in Ĝ of irreducible unitarizable πₙ, then τ occurs in πₙ|_K for all but finitely many n (Gan–Savin Lemma 11.4).
hypotheses: G locally profinite; π, πₙ irreducible unitarizable (points of Ĝ).
proofSteps: Take a unit vector v in the τ-isotypic part of π, so ⟪v, π(e_τ)v⟫ = 1 for the K-type projector e_τ = π(f_τ) (smooth-vectors-unitary; Gan–Savin's f_τ needs the factor dim τ, sourceIssues E1).
By the definition of limit points there are unit vₙ with ptCoeff πₙ vₙ → ptCoeff π v uniformly on K; integrating against f_τ gives ⟪vₙ, πₙ(e_τ)vₙ⟫ → 1.
Hence πₙ(e_τ) ≠ 0 for large n, i.e. τ occurs in πₙ.
acceptance: For K-spherical π (τ trivial), every limit of the πₙ that is K-spherical forces the πₙ to be K-spherical eventually.
The transfer goes only from the limit to the sequence: spherical complementary series of SL₂(ℚ_p) have SL₂(ℤ_p)-fixed vectors, while their limit point St has none.

sources.match: If an irreducible unitarizable π containing the K-type τ is a limit point of irreducible πₙ, then τ occurs in πₙ for almost all n, by integrating the converging coefficients against f_τ.

nodes.title: Rodier's heredity of genericity
nodes.statement: Let G be quasi-split reductive over F, B = TU a Borel subgroup, ψ a generic character of U (SR.2.3 whittaker-functionals), P = MN a standard parabolic and σ an admissible finite-length representation of M. Then dim Hom_U(i_P σ, ψ) = dim Hom_{U∩M}(σ, ψ|_{U∩M}) for a compatible choice of ψ; in particular i_P σ is ψ-generic iff σ is, and for irreducible generic σ the induced representation i_P σ has exactly one ψ-generic irreducible subquotient, occurring with multiplicity one.
hypotheses: G quasi-split; ψ generic, compatible with the Levi M (Shahidi's normalisation of the splitting).
proofSteps: Filter i_P σ by the Bruhat cells P\PwB (SR.2 mackey-filtration, geometric-lemma); only the open cell supports ψ-equivariant functionals for generic ψ, giving the dimension formula.

Exactness of the twisted Jacquet functor V ↦ V_{U,ψ} (SR.2.3, coinvariants of the twist) makes generic multiplicity additive in short exact sequences, so a constituent count of one gives uniqueness of the generic subquotient.
acceptance: For GL₂(ℚ_p), i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) has the unique generic constituent St, and the trivial constituent is not generic.
For every unitary character χ of T, i_B χ is generic.

sources.match: Heiermann–Opdam recall, by Rodier's theorem, that the induced representation i_P τ_ν of a generic τ has a unique ψ-generic irreducible subquotient.
Each unramified principal series X(χ) has a unique irreducible generic subquotient.

sources.locator: F. Rodier, Whittaker models for admissible representations of reductive p-adic split groups, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 26 (1973) (not read)
sources.match: The heredity theorem.

nodes.title: Heiermann–Opdam: generic representations are standard modules
nodes.statement: Let G be quasi-split reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero. Let P = MN be a standard parabolic, τ an irreducible tempered generic representation of M and ν in the open positive chamber a_M^{*+} (SR.3.3 langlands-classification, Langlands convention). Then the Langlands quotient J(τ, ν) of the standard module i_P(τ_ν) is generic iff i_P(τ_ν) is irreducible (the standard module conjecture). Consequently every irreducible generic representation of G is isomorphic to an irreducible standard module i_P(τ_ν), with τ tempered generic and ν ∈ a_M^{*+}, and its differential is a positive combination Σ_{α∈Δ∖S} s_α ϖ_α of fundamental weights (Gan–Savin, proof of Proposition 11.2).
hypotheses: F a p-adic field of characteristic zero; G quasi-split; the Langlands classification of SR.3.3 with its Harish–Chandra tempered-support hypothesis.
proofSteps: Heiermann–Opdam prove holomorphy of the local coefficient in the negative chamber and the tempered L-function conjecture (HO Theorem 1.1); with Heiermann–Muić this gives the standard module conjecture (HO Corollary 1.2).

If π is irreducible generic, write π = J(τ, ν) by the Langlands classification; i_P(τ_ν) has π as a generic subquotient, so τ is generic (rodier-heredity), and by the standard module conjecture i_P(τ_ν) is irreducible, hence equal to π.
The positive-chamber condition is ν = Σ_{α∈Δ∖S} s_α ϖ_α with s_α > 0, S the simple roots of M.
acceptance: For GL₂(ℚ_p), the generic representation i_B(|·|^{1/4} ⊗ |·|^{−1/4}) is an irreducible standard module, while the non-generic trivial representation is the Langlands quotient of the reducible i_B(δ_B^{1/2}).

sources.match: For quasi-split G over a p-adic field of characteristic zero, the local coefficient is holomorphic in the negative chamber; consequently the Langlands quotient of a standard module with tempered generic data is generic iff the standard module is irreducible.
By [HO] every generic representation is isomorphic to a standard module Ind_P^G(τ), τ = τ°·χ with τ° tempered and χ unramified positive with differential Σ s_α ϖ_α, s_α > 0.

nodes.title: Limits of generic unitary representations
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G. with 𝐆 split simple. Let δ be generic unitarizable and (πₙ) generic unitarizable with δ ∈ L[πₙ]. After passing to a subsequence there are a parabolic P = MN and standard modules i_P(τₙ) with: πₙ ≅ i_P(τₙ) for all n; the characters of τₙ converge weakly to the character of a (possibly reducible) representation τ of M; and δ is a subquotient of i_P(τ). In particular τ is generic (Gan–Savin Proposition 11.2).
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 connected reductive over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero (Gan–Savin take 𝐆 split simple), complex coefficients, a fixed Haar measure dg on G.
𝐆 split simple, as in Gan–Savin; δ, πₙ generic unitarizable.
proofSteps: By heiermann-opdam-standard-module each πₙ ≅ i_{Pₙ}(τₙ) with τₙ = τₙ° · χₙ; finitely many standard parabolics, so after a subsequence P is constant.

By tadic-tempered-limits a subsequence of τₙ° has weakly convergent characters with limit τ°; unitarity of πₙ bounds the differentials dχₙ, because the coefficients of πₙ are bounded by ‖v‖² while along the negative cone they are asymptotic to combinations of the exponents of the Jacquet modules (SR.2 casselman-pairing), which grow with dχₙ; so a further subsequence has χₙ → χ; put τ = τ° · χ.

The characters of i_P(τₙ) converge to that of i_P(τ) (character-weak-convergence, induction); by milicic-limits the limit points of (πₙ) are the constituents of i_P(τ), so δ is a subquotient; δ generic forces τ generic (rodier-heredity).
acceptance: For PGL₂(ℚ_p) and the generic complementary series πₙ = i_B(|·|^{sₙ} ⊗ |·|^{−sₙ}) with sₙ → 1/2, the generic limit point is St, a subquotient of i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) = lim i_B(τₙ).

sources.match: A generic unitarizable limit point δ of generic unitarizable πₙ is, after passing to a subsequence, a subquotient of Ind_P^G(τ) where πₙ ≅ Ind_P^G(τₙ) are standard modules whose inducing characters converge weakly to that of τ; the proof combines [HO], [Ta1] and Theorem 11.1.

nodes.title: Discrete series are isolated in the tempered dual
nodes.statement: Let G be a reductive group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero with compact centre (or work with a fixed unitary central character). Every irreducible square-integrable representation δ (SR.3.3) is an isolated point of the tempered part Ĝ_temp of Ĝ with the induced Fell topology: no sequence of tempered irreducible representations not isomorphic to δ converges to [δ].
hypotheses: F of characteristic zero, as in Gan–Savin; G with compact centre, or all representations with a fixed unitary central character.
proofSteps: Use SRup SR.3.3 harish-chandra-tempered-support to express each irreducible tempered representation as a constituent of induction from a discrete series of a Levi. This gives decomposition and uniqueness, not a description of Fell neighbourhoods.

The missing input is the finite-level local structure of the tempered dual: after fixing a compact-open type near δ, a convergent family is controlled by finitely many induction data with compact unitary-unramified parameter spaces, and the discrete-series point cannot occur as a limit from a proper-Levi component. Supply the precise theorem and proof before using this step; Bernstein-centre convergence alone does not imply it.

Conditional on that input, only the G-Levi discrete-series family can approach δ. For compact centre the ordinary unitary-unramified character group of G is trivial; with fixed central character the allowed twisting fibre is finite. Removing its other points isolates δ.

Ordinary unramified characters here use the subgroup generated by all compact subgroups (SRup SR.3.1, target unramified-characters). They differ from weakly unramified characters. The statement remains a target with its spectral-topology proof prerequisite recorded as a gap.
acceptance: For PGL₂(ℚ_p) the Steinberg representation is not a limit of unitary principal series i_B(|·|^{itₙ} ⊗ |·|^{−itₙ}): their limits are unitary principal series, which do not contain St.
Isolation holds only in the tempered dual: in the full unitary dual of PGL₂(ℚ_p) the Steinberg representation is a limit of complementary series (SRU.4 steinberg-isolated, rank-one non-example).

sources.locator: §11.1, proof of Proposition 11.3, pp. 32–33; §10.3, proof of Lemma 10.8, p. 30
sources.match: Gan–Savin use that square-integrable representations are isolated in the tempered dual to assume the approximating representations nontempered.

sources.locator: M. Tadić, Geometry of dual spaces of reductive groups (non-Archimedean case), J. Analyse Math. 51 (1988) (not read)
sources.match: The description of the topology of the tempered dual that the citing paper relies on.

nodes.title: The Steinberg representation of a finite reductive group
nodes.statement: Let Γ = 𝐆(𝔽_q) for a split connected reductive group 𝐆 over 𝔽_q, with Borel subgroup B = B(𝔽_q), Weyl group W, simple reflections S and N = |Φ⁺|. The Steinberg representation st_Γ is the irreducible complex representation whose character is Σ_{J⊆S} (−1)^{|J|} Ind_{P_J}^{Γ} 1 (P_J the standard parabolic subgroups); it has degree q^N, its B-fixed line is acted on by the Iwahori–Hecke algebra End_Γ(Ind_B^Γ 1) through the sign character T_s ↦ −1 (s ∈ S), and it is the unique constituent of Ind_B^Γ 1 with this property. For the reductive p-adic G of SRU.4, st_G denotes its inflation to K = 𝐆(O) along K → 𝐆(𝔽_q).
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over 𝔽_q; complex coefficients.
proofSteps: The constituents of Ind_B^Γ 1 correspond to the irreducible modules of H(W, q) = End_Γ(Ind_B^Γ 1), whose basis T_w (w ∈ W) comes from the Bruhat decomposition Γ = ⊔ BwB (ReductiveGroups layer 7) with the quadratic and braid relations. For K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, K/I ≅ Γ/B via the reduction K → Γ, so H(W, q) ≅ H(K, I), the finite part of the Iwahori–Matsumoto presentation of H(G, I) generated by the T_w, w ∈ W (SR.1 iwahori-matsumoto). The sign character T_s ↦ −1 gives a constituent st_Γ.
The alternating sum Σ_J (−1)^{|J|} Ind_{P_J} 1 is the character of this constituent (Solomon–Tits: it is the top homology of the Tits building); its degree is the index-weighted alternating sum, q^N.

Inflation along the reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), surjective with kernel the positive radical K⁺ (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 reductive-quotient-of-special-fibre; the special fibre is 𝐆_{𝔽_q} because K is hyperspecial, RG2.3 hyperspecial-vertices), gives a smooth irreducible representation of K.

The finite-Hecke sign character and its q^{|Φ⁺|} degree are independently supported by CIK71 §4, pp. 94–95. Identifying it with the alternating parabolic character additionally uses the Solomon/Coxeter-complex identity; that combinatorial input is recorded in the finite-Steinberg gap below.
acceptance: For Γ = GL₂(𝔽_q), Ind_B^Γ 1 = 1 ⊕ st_Γ with dim st_Γ = q.
For Γ a split torus, st_Γ is the trivial representation.

sources.match: For a special maximal compact K with quotient G(𝔽_q), st_G is the inflation to K of the Steinberg representation of the finite group G(𝔽_q); the restriction of the Steinberg representation of G to K contains st_G.

The Iwahori–Matsumoto involution of the Iwahori-spherical category preserves hermitian and unitary modules, exchanges spherical and generic modules, and takes the trivial representation to the Steinberg representation.

The sign character of the finite Hecke algebra determines a unique irreducible constituent of the flag permutation representation, of degree q to the number of positive roots; this is Steinberg’s representation.

uses.how: st_G is the K-type detecting genericity and the unique Iwahori K-type of St_G
representations containing st_G are generic

nodes.title: The Iwahori K-type of the Steinberg representation
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r. The restriction of the Steinberg representation St_G (SR.3.4) to K contains st_G with multiplicity one, and st_G is the only irreducible K-type of St_G having nonzero I-fixed vectors.
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r.
proofSteps: St_G^I is one-dimensional (SR.3.4 steinberg). It is the I-fixed part of C^∞(B\G)/Σ_{B⊊P} C^∞(P\G): by the Bruhat decomposition C^∞(B\G)^I = ℂ[B\G/I] is the regular module of H(K, I) ≅ H(W, q), the subspaces C^∞(P_J\G)^I are the modules induced from the trivial character of H(W_J, q), and the quotient by their sum over J ≠ ∅ is the sign character (Solomon–Kilmoyer).

For any smooth V, V^I = (V^{K⁺})^{B(𝔽_q)} with K⁺ the positive radical of K (finite-steinberg); the K-types of V with I-fixed vectors are the constituents of Ind_B^Γ 1 occurring in V^{K⁺}, detected by the H(W, q)-module V^I.
The sign module corresponds to st_Γ (finite-steinberg), with multiplicity dim St_G^I = 1.
acceptance: For GL₂(ℚ_p), St restricted to GL₂(ℤ_p) contains the q-dimensional st of GL₂(𝔽_p) once, and no K-type of St with I-fixed vectors other than st.

sources.match: The restriction of the Steinberg representation σ to K contains st_G, and st_G is the unique K-type of σ with Iwahori-fixed vectors.

nodes.title: Barbasch–Moy: the Steinberg K-type detects genericity
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r. An irreducible admissible representation π of G whose restriction to K contains st_G is generic (admits a nonzero Whittaker functional for a generic character, SR.2.3). More precisely, for irreducible π with π^I ≠ 0, π is generic iff the H(K, I)-module π^I contains the sign character, iff π|_K contains st_G (Barbasch–Moy).
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r.
π irreducible admissible.
proofSteps: st_G has nonzero I-fixed vectors, so π^I ≠ 0 and π lies in the Iwahori block (SR.3.4 borel-casselman-block); π^I is a simple H(G, I)-module.

Barbasch–Moy identify the Whittaker functionals on Iwahori-spherical π with the sign-isotypic part of π^I under the finite Hecke algebra: the Gelfand–Graev representation's I-fixed part is the induced module of the sign character of H(K, I) to H(G, I) (Barbasch–Moy 1994).
Containing st_G is equivalent to the sign character occurring in π^I (steinberg-k-types).
acceptance: The trivial representation does not contain st_G and is not generic; the Steinberg representation contains st_G and is generic.
For GL₂(ℚ_p), an irreducible unramified principal series i_B(χ) contains st_G (its Iwahori invariants are the regular H(W, q)-module) and is generic.

sources.match: Representations containing st_G are generic, by [BM].
Barbasch–Moy relate genericity of Iwahori-spherical modules to the Hecke algebra; for adjoint G a subquotient of X(χ) is both generic and spherical iff it is all of X(χ).

sources.locator: D. Barbasch and A. Moy, Whittaker models with an Iwahori fixed vector, Contemp. Math. 177 (1994) 101–105 (not read)
sources.match: The cited source.

nodes.title: Rodier's decomposition of the principal series containing the Steinberg representation
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r. Let χ = δ_B^{1/2} (normalised induction), so that i_B(χ) has the Steinberg representation as a subrepresentation and the trivial representation as its unique irreducible quotient. Then i_B(χ) has exactly 2^r irreducible subquotients π_J, J ⊆ Δ (simple roots), each with multiplicity one, π_∅ = 1 and π_Δ = St_G (up to the convention fixing which end is which), and the exponents of the normalised Jacquet module r_B(π_J) are the w·χ for w in the set of Weyl group elements whose descent set is determined by J (Rodier; Casselman).
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r.
proofSteps: χ = δ_B^{1/2} is regular, so r_B(i_B χ) has the |W| distinct exponents w·χ (SR.2 principal-series-jacquet). Since r_B(St_G) = δ_B^{1/2} (SR.3.4 steinberg), first adjointness (SR.2 first-adjointness) embeds St_G in i_B(δ_B^{1/2}); dually the trivial representation is its quotient.

Rodier’s theorem gives multiplicity-one irreducible constituents indexed by subsets of the simple roots, with the required Jacquet exponents. The proof is not obtained by taking a product of rank-one submodule lattices: rank-one intertwiner relations do not imply that assertion. The exact combinatorial theorem is an explicit prerequisite gap.
The exponent sets are read off from which intertwining operators T_{s_α} vanish on the constituent (Casselman 1980, Theorem 3.1).
acceptance: For PGL₂, r = 1 and i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) has the two constituents 1 and St.
For PGL₃, i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) has four constituents, 1, St and two further infinite-dimensional ones, each with multiplicity one.

sources.match: By Rodier [Ro], Ind_B^G(χ) has 2^r irreducible subquotients whose exponents, hence matrix-coefficient asymptotics, are known.
For regular χ the intertwining operators T_w and the factors c_α(χ) control irreducibility of the unramified principal series.

sources.locator: F. Rodier, Decomposition of principal series for reductive p-adic groups and the Langlands' classification, in Operator algebras and group representations II (Neptun 1980), Pitman 1984, 86–94 (not read)
sources.match: The cited source.

nodes.title: The Howe–Moore theorem over nonarchimedean local fields
nodes.statement: Let 𝐆 be connected, almost simple and isotropic over a nonarchimedean local field F (any characteristic), G = 𝐆(F) and G⁺ the normal subgroup generated by the unipotent radicals of F-parabolic subgroups (G⁺ = G for 𝐆 simply connected; G/G⁺ is compact abelian in general, and finite in characteristic zero). If π is a strongly continuous unitary representation of G with no nonzero G⁺-invariant vector, then every coefficient g ↦ ⟪w, π(g)v⟫ vanishes at infinity on G. In particular, an infinite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation of G has coefficients vanishing at infinity.
hypotheses: 𝐆 almost F-simple and F-isotropic; π strongly continuous unitary without G⁺-invariant vectors.
proofSteps: Cartan decomposition reduces coefficient decay to escape in a positive chamber. Uniformity is needed only for compact K-orbits of fixed v and w and follows from finite ε-nets and unitarity. Uniform decay over the entire unit ball would be false.

Use the full Howe–Moore contraction/Mautner lemma to show every weak cluster vector along an escaping chamber sequence is G⁺-fixed. The contracted root groups alone do not generate their opposites; that propagation is a nonroutine part of the theorem, recorded as a gap below. CCLTV §1, pp. 1–2, confirms the G⁺ theorem in arbitrary local-field characteristic; its separate relative Theorem 1.4 is characteristic zero only.
The hypothesis forces the weak cluster vectors to vanish, hence all coefficients tend to zero at infinity.

For an irreducible π, H^{G⁺} is closed invariant, so is either zero or H. In the latter case π factors through compact abelian G/G⁺ and is one-dimensional. Thus an infinite-dimensional irreducible has no G⁺-fixed vector. For PGL_p over 𝔽_q((t)), F×/(F×)^p illustrates why finiteness must not be asserted in positive characteristic.
acceptance: For G = SL₂(ℚ_p), the coefficients of the Steinberg representation (square-integrable) and of every unitary principal series vanish at infinity; the trivial representation is excluded by the invariant-vector hypothesis.

For G = PGL₂(ℚ_p) the unitary character g ↦ (−1)^{v_p(det g)} is a nontrivial one-dimensional unitary representation whose coefficient does not vanish at infinity; it is trivial on G⁺, as the hypothesis requires.

sources.match: The subgroup generated by unipotent elements in a simple algebraic group over a local field has the Howe–Moore property (citing Howe–Moore); for groups over ℚ_p, (G, S⁺) has the relative Howe–Moore property when S⁺ is generated by the unipotents of a simple algebraic group.

sources.locator: §11.1, end of the proof of Proposition 11.3, p. 33
sources.match: By a theorem of Howe and Moore, subquotients whose matrix coefficients do not decay at infinity are not unitarizable unless trivial.
No unbounded region of spherical parameters is unitary, citing Howe–Moore.

sources.locator: R. Howe and C. C. Moore, Asymptotic properties of unitary representations, J. Funct. Anal. 32 (1979) 72–96, Theorem 5.1 (not read)
sources.match: The original theorem.

nodes.title: Unitary constituents of the Steinberg principal series
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r. The only unitarizable irreducible subquotients of the principal series i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) of rodier-steinberg-series are the trivial representation and the Steinberg representation.
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r.
proofSteps: The trivial representation is unitarizable; St_G is square-integrable, hence unitarizable (SR.3.3 square-integrable-tempered).

For J ≠ ∅, Δ, the constituent π_J is infinite-dimensional and some exponent w·χ of r_B(π_J) has absolute value ≥ 1 on a ray of the negative cone (rodier-steinberg-series); by Casselman's pairing (SR.2 casselman-pairing) the K-finite coefficients of π_J along that ray are asymptotic to a nonzero combination of those exponents, so they do not vanish at infinity.
An infinite-dimensional unitarizable π_J would have coefficients vanishing at infinity (howe-moore), a contradiction.
acceptance: For PGL₂ the statement is empty beyond 1 and St, which are the only constituents.
For PGL₃ the two intermediate constituents of i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) are not unitarizable.

sources.locator: §11.1, end of the proof of Proposition 11.3, p. 33
sources.match: The exponents of Rodier's subquotients determine the asymptotics of their matrix coefficients; those other than the Steinberg representation do not decay, so by Howe–Moore the only unitarizable subquotients are the trivial and the Steinberg representation.

nodes.title: The Steinberg representation is isolated
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r. If r ≥ 2, the Steinberg representation St_G is an isolated point of the unitary dual Ĝ (Gan–Savin Proposition 11.3). For r = 1 (SL₂, PGL₂) the statement is false: St_G is a limit point of the spherical complementary series.
hypotheses: G = 𝐆(F) with 𝐆 a split, almost simple (Chevalley) group over a p-adic field F of characteristic zero, residue field 𝔽_q, hyperspecial K = 𝐆(O) with reduction K → 𝐆(𝔽_q), Iwahori subgroup I = preimage of a Borel B(𝔽_q), rank r.
proofSteps: Suppose [St] ∈ L[πₙ] with πₙ irreducible unitarizable, πₙ ≇ St. By k-types-persist, st_G occurs in πₙ for n large, so πₙ is generic (barbasch-moy-genericity), and the gan-savin-generic-limits apply: after a subsequence πₙ ≅ i_P(τₙ), τₙ → τ, St a subquotient of i_P(τ), and every subquotient of i_P(τ) is a limit point (milicic-limits), hence unitarizable.

πₙ is eventually nontempered (discrete-series-isolated-tempered), so P ≠ G. By fell-convergence-bernstein-centre every subquotient of i_P(τ) has the cuspidal support of St, i.e. lies in i_B(δ_B^{1/2}).
If P = B, all 2^r ≥ 4 constituents of i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) would be unitarizable, contradicting steinberg-series-unitary.

If B ⊊ P ⊊ G: τ has Iwahori-spherical cuspidal support because i_P(τ) has the cuspidal support of St; hence τ is Iwahori-spherical. Within that block τ is generic, so (barbasch-moy-genericity for M) st_M is a (K ∩ M)-type of τ; by the Iwasawa decomposition G = QK for a minimal parabolic Q ⊆ P (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4), hence G = PK, i_P(τ)|_K = Ind_{K∩P}^K(τ|_{K∩M}) contains the inflation of the finite induced representation Ind_{P(𝔽_q)}^{Γ}(st_{M(𝔽_q)}), whose B(𝔽_q)-fixed vectors form the H(W, q)-module induced from the sign character of H(W_M, q). It has dimension [W : W_M] > 1, contains the sign character once and the trivial character not at all (W_M ≠ 1), so it has an irreducible constituent different from both; this is a K-type with I-fixed vectors other than st_G and other than the trivial K-type. The constituent of i_P(τ) carrying it is unitarizable, is not St (steinberg-k-types) and not 1, contradicting steinberg-series-unitary. Gan–Savin call this step easy; the expansion here is the finite-Hecke-algebra computation.
acceptance: For PGL₂(ℚ_p) the complementary series i_B(|·|^{s} ⊗ |·|^{−s}), 0 < s < 1/2, converge as s → 1/2 to both 1 and St in the Fell topology, so St is not isolated in rank one.
For G₂(ℚ₅) (rank 2) St is isolated; this is the input of the counterexample to the subsequence form of Gan–Savin Proposition 11.6 (SRU.1 gan-savin-closure).

sources.match: If rank G ≥ 2 the Steinberg representation is isolated in the unitary dual; the proof uses Lemma 11.4, Barbasch–Moy, Proposition 11.2, isolation of discrete series in the tempered dual, Tadić's Bernstein-centre convergence, Rodier's decomposition and Howe–Moore.

nodes.title: Supercuspidal representations are isolated
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) be reductive over a nonarchimedean local field with compact centre. Every irreducible unitarizable supercuspidal representation σ of G is an isolated point of Ĝ. (With noncompact centre the same holds in the subset of Ĝ with a fixed unitary central character.)
hypotheses: Z(G) compact, or a fixed unitary central character.
proofSteps: By the Bernstein decomposition (SR.3 bernstein-decomposition, cuspidal-splitting) the component of σ is {σ ⊗ ψ : ψ unramified}, which for compact centre is {σ} up to isomorphism; let e be the idempotent of the Bernstein centre cutting it out and K a compact open subgroup with σ^K ≠ 0. Then f := e ∗ 1_K (normalised) lies in C_c^∞(G).
For an irreducible unitarizable π, π(f) ≠ 0 iff π is in the component of σ and π^K ≠ 0, iff π ≅ σ.
The set {x ∈ Ĝ : rep x (f) ≠ 0} is open in the Fell topology (fell-topology, UnitaryDual.isOpen_setOf_apply_ne_zero), so {[σ]} is open.
acceptance: For PGL₂(ℚ_p), every depth-zero supercuspidal representation is isolated, while the unitary principal series are not.
For ℚ_p^× (noncompact centre) a unitary character is not isolated in the full unitary dual, being a limit of unramified twists; it is isolated among characters with a fixed value at p.

sources.match: Supercuspidal representations and the Steinberg representation are isolated in the unitary dual, which lets Corollary 11.7 produce the global representation.
The cuspidal component of an irreducible cuspidal σ is the set of its unramified twists, split off by an idempotent of the centre.

nodes.title: Satake parameters, real parts and the spherical principal series
nodes.statement: Let k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting). For s ∈ T^∨ = Hom(X^∨, ℂ^×), χ_s := s ∘ val_T : T(k) → ℂ^× with ⟨val_T(t), λ⟩ = val_k(λ(t)) (Ciubotaru–Harris (6.1)); X(s) := i_B(χ_s) (normalised, SR.2) and L(s) its unique K-spherical irreducible subquotient; s ↦ L(s) is a bijection from W-orbits in T^∨ to irreducible K-spherical representations, s being the Satake parameter (SR.4 spherical-parameter, satake-isomorphism, with complex coefficients and the positive square root q^{1/2} ∈ ℂ fixing normalised induction). Polar decomposition T^∨ = T^∨_ℝ · T^∨_c with T^∨_ℝ = X ⊗ ℝ_{>0}, T^∨_c = X ⊗ S¹; every s is uniquely s = s_c·s_ν with s_c ∈ T^∨_c, ν ∈ t^∨_ℝ = X ⊗ ℝ and s_ν = exp(ν log q); s_ν is a real Satake parameter, X(ν) := X(s_ν), L(ν) := L(s_ν). C₀ = {ν : ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ≥ 0 for α ∈ Π}, C_{0,h} = {ν ∈ C₀ : w₀ν = −ν} (hermitian locus), A₀ = {ν ∈ C₀ : ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ < 1} (γ^∨ the highest coroot), ρ = half the sum of positive roots; the trivial representation is L(ρ). Convention: with (6.1), χ_{s_ν}(λ^∨(ϖ)) = q^{⟨λ^∨, ν⟩}, so for dominant ν the spherical L(ν) is the unique irreducible subrepresentation of X(ν) (and the unique quotient of X(−ν)); Barbasch–Ciubotaru's χ_ν(τ(a)) = |a|^{⟨τ, ν⟩} differs by ν ↦ −ν, which changes no statement of SRU.5–SRU.7 because L(ν) and L(−ν) are hermitian duals and unitarity is preserved (sourceIssues E2).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: X(s)^K is one-dimensional by the Iwasawa decomposition (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4), so X(s) has exactly one K-spherical constituent L(s) (SR.2 induced-invariants).
The Hecke character of L(s) is evaluation of the Satake transform at s; the Satake isomorphism identifies H(G, K) with ℂ[T^∨]^W (SR.4), so L(s) ≅ L(s') iff s' ∈ W·s.
Polar decomposition is that of ℂ^× = ℝ_{>0} × S¹ coordinatewise in X ⊗ ℂ^×.

Sign of the convention: val_T(λ^∨(ϖ)) = λ^∨ gives χ_{s_ν}(λ^∨(ϖ)) = q^{⟨λ^∨, ν⟩}; for PGL₂ and ν = ρ this is δ_B^{−1/2}, and i_B(δ_B^{−1/2}) = Ind_B 1 has the trivial representation as subrepresentation (SR.3.4 steinberg).
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ the Satake parameters are s ∈ ℂ^× modulo s ↦ s⁻¹; the trivial representation is L(q^{1/2}) = L(ρ), and L(1) = X(1) is the unitary spherical principal series at the centre.
For every s, L(s) ≅ L(w·s) for w ∈ W, and s = s_c s_ν with s_c = 1 iff s ∈ T^∨_ℝ.

sources.locator: §6, (6.1)–(6.6) and the paragraphs between them, pp. 16–18
sources.match: Ciubotaru–Harris fix the split adjoint setting, the character χ_s = s ∘ val_T, the unitarily induced X(s) with unique spherical subquotient L(s), the bijection with W-orbits, the polar decomposition s = s_c s_ν, real Satake parameters, C₀, the hermitian locus and the fundamental alcove; L(ρ) is the trivial representation.

Barbasch–Ciubotaru parametrise real unramified characters by ν ∈ X^*(H) ⊗ ℝ through χ_ν(τ(a)) = |a|^{⟨τ, ν⟩}, the opposite sign; for dominant χ the spherical L(χ) is the unique irreducible quotient of X(χ).

uses.how: every statement about generic unitary spherical representations is phrased in Satake parameters s = s_c s_ν
the global proof records ν_w(σ) = log_q|ι(s_w(σ))| at unramified places

nodes.title: Half-integral real parts and geometric Satake parameters
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, let (V, ρ_V) be a finite-dimensional representation of g^∨ (equivalently of G^∨). A real parameter ν ∈ t^∨_ℝ is half-integral with respect to V if ⟨χ, ν⟩ ∈ ½ℤ for every weight χ of V; the Satake parameter s = s_c s_ν is then called geometric with respect to V (Ciubotaru–Harris Definition 6.3). This is a condition on the real part only, not algebraicity of s_c. For a fixed 0 ≤ ε < ½, C₀^{½+ε} := {ν ∈ C₀ : ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ε + ½ℤ for all α^∨ ∈ Φ^∨} ((6.11)); C₀^{½} is the set of ν ∈ C₀ half-integral for the adjoint representation. In fundamental-weight coordinates ν = Σ νᵢ ωᵢ, ν ∈ C₀^{½} iff every νᵢ ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0}.
hypotheses: V finite-dimensional; ν real.
proofSteps: Weights of the adjoint representation are the roots of g^∨, i.e. the coroots α^∨ of G; so adjoint half-integrality is ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ½ℤ for all coroots, equivalently for the simple ones.
For ν dominant, ⟨αᵢ^∨, ν⟩ = νᵢ in fundamental-weight coordinates.
acceptance: ρ is half-integral for every representation of G^∨ (its pairings with weights are half-integers), so the trivial representation L(ρ) is geometric for all V.
The real part ν of a tempered spherical representation is 0, half-integral for every V.

sources.match: ν is half-integral with respect to V when all its pairings with weights of V lie in ½ℤ, and then s is called geometric; C₀^{½+ε} collects the dominant ν whose coroot pairings lie in ε + ½ℤ.

uses.how: Weil-number eigenvalues of Frobenius on the local systems L(π, τ) force half-integrality of ν_w for the weights of τ
the test that eliminates nonzero real parts

nodes.title: Tempered spherical representations
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, L(s) is tempered iff its real part ν is 0; in that case L(s) = X(s) is an irreducible summand of a principal series unitarily induced from a unitary character of B (Ciubotaru–Harris Lemma 5.2, in local form).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: If ν=0, χ_s is unitary and normalised induction is tempered. In the adjoint setting of real-satake-parameter, irreducibility follows from the unramified irreducibility criterion; hence its spherical constituent is tempered. No argument uses unitarizability alone to deduce irreducibility.

Conversely use the spherical Langlands classification and Casselman’s tempered exponent criterion, precisely as in CH26 Lemma 5.2, pp. 12–13: a nonzero dominant real part gives a nonzero positive Langlands exponent, incompatible with temperedness. The Jacquet exponent set of an individual spherical constituent need not be Weyl stable.
acceptance: For PGL₂(ℚ_p), the spherical L(s) is tempered iff |s| = 1; the trivial representation L(q^{1/2}) is not tempered.

sources.match: A spherical local component is tempered iff its real Satake part vanishes, and is then a summand of a principal series unitarily induced from a unitary character of the minimal parabolic; the proof uses Casselman's criterion.

nodes.title: Irreducibility of unramified principal series
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter: (1) for s regular (trivial stabiliser in W), X(s) is irreducible iff α^∨(s) ≠ q^{±1} for every root α (Casselman 1980 Proposition 3.5(b)); (2) for general s and G adjoint (so G^∨ simply connected and every centraliser Z_{G^∨}(s) connected), X(s) is irreducible iff α^∨(s) ≠ q^{±1} for every root α (Kato's criterion; its second condition, that W_s be generated by reflections, holds automatically); (3) for a real dominant ν, X(ν) is irreducible iff ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ≠ 1 for every positive coroot α^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris p. 17; Barbasch–Ciubotaru §3.1).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: (1): Casselman's intertwining operators T_w with T_{w⁻¹} ∘ T_w = c_{w⁻¹}(wχ)c_w(χ) and c_α(χ) = (1 − q⁻¹χ(a_α))/(1 − χ(a_α)) for split groups (Casselman 1980 Theorem 3.1); irreducibility iff the product over all positive roots is nonzero (Proposition 3.5(b)).
(2): Kato extends (1) to singular s; for G adjoint, Steinberg's theorem makes Z_{G^∨}(s) connected and W_s its Weyl group, generated by reflections.
(3): for real dominant ν, α^∨(s_ν) = q^{⟨α^∨, ν⟩} with ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ≥ 0 for positive α, so only the value 1 can occur.
acceptance: For PGL₂ with s=diag(t,t⁻¹), reducibility occurs exactly at t²=q^{±1}. At t=+q^{1/2} the Jordan–Hölder constituents are 1 and St; at t=−q^{1/2} both are twisted by the unramified quadratic character. These endpoint principal series are nonsplit extensions, not Hilbert direct sums.
For PGL₂ and the real parameter ν with ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ = 1, X(ν) contains the trivial and Steinberg representations.

sources.locator: §3, Theorem 3.1 (p. 397) and Proposition 3.5(b) (p. 401, page image checked)
sources.match: For regular unramified χ, Ind(χ) is irreducible iff c_{w_ℓ}(w_ℓχ)c_{w_ℓ}(χ) ≠ 0, i.e. no root value χ(a_α) equals q^{±1} in the split case.
The reducibility points of X(s) go back to Casselman for regular s; for real ν, X(ν) = L(ν) iff ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ≠ 1 for all positive coroots.
For dominant χ, X(χ) is reducible iff ⟨α, χ⟩ = 1 for some positive α.

sources.locator: S. Kato, Irreducibility of principal series representations for Hecke algebras of affine type, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 28 (1981) (not read)
sources.match: Kato's criterion for singular parameters.

nodes.title: Generic spherical representations
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, each X(s) has a unique generic irreducible subquotient (Rodier), and L(s) is generic iff X(s) is irreducible, i.e. iff L(s) = X(s) (Barbasch–Moy; Ciubotaru–Harris p. 17). Consequently a tempered L(s) is generic (Ciubotaru–Harris Corollary 5.7, local part).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: Uniqueness of the generic constituent: SRU.3 rodier-heredity for P = B.
If X(s) is irreducible, L(s) = X(s) is generic (every principal series is generic).

If L(s) is generic, its Iwahori-fixed H(K, I)-module contains both the trivial character (spherical) and the sign character (generic, SRU.4 barbasch-moy-genericity); for adjoint G Barbasch–Moy show this forces L(s) = X(s) (Barbasch–Ciubotaru §1.2, [BM4]).
Tempered spherical: ν = 0 (spherical-tempered-criterion), so |α^∨(s)| = 1 ≠ q^{±1} and X(s) is irreducible (unramified-principal-series-irreducibility), hence generic.
acceptance: The trivial representation L(ρ) is not generic (rank ≥ 1), and X(ρ) is reducible.
Every L(s_c) with s_c compact is generic and equal to X(s_c).

sources.match: By [BM2] the spherical L(s) is generic iff X(s) = L(s); tempered spherical representations of split adjoint groups are the full principal series and hence generic.
Each X(χ) has a unique generic subquotient; for adjoint G a subquotient is both generic and spherical iff it is the whole X(χ).

nodes.title: Hermitian spherical representations
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, L(s) admits a nonzero G-invariant hermitian form iff some w ∈ W maps s to s̄⁻¹ (Barbasch–Ciubotaru §1.2); for a real dominant ν this means w₀ν = −ν (Ciubotaru–Harris (6.5)). When w₀ = −1 (types A₁, B, C, D_{2m}, G₂, F₄, E₇, E₈) every real ν is hermitian; Ciubotaru–Harris list B, C, G₂, F₄, E₇, E₈.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: An invariant hermitian form is an isomorphism L(s) → conj(L(s)~); the contragredient of L(s) is L(s⁻¹) and its complex conjugate L(s̄⁻¹), so the condition is L(s) ≅ L(s̄⁻¹), i.e. s̄⁻¹ ∈ W·s (real-satake-parameter).
For s = s_ν real, s̄⁻¹ = s_{−ν}; for dominant ν, −ν ∈ W·ν iff −ν = w₀ν.
acceptance: For PGL₃ (w₀ ≠ −1) the real dominant ν = ω₁ is not hermitian.
For PGL₂ every real ν is hermitian.

sources.match: L(χ) admits an invariant hermitian form iff wχ = χ⁻¹ for some w; for real dominant χ, X(χ) is hermitian iff w₀χ = −χ.
Ciubotaru–Harris state the hermitian criterion w₀(ν) = −ν and its automatic validity for types B, C, G₂, F₄, E₇, E₈.

nodes.title: The generic unitary spherical region
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, U₀^g := {ν ∈ C₀ : ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ≠ 1 for every α^∨ ∈ Φ^{∨,+} and L(ν) is unitary} parametrises the generic spherical unitary representations with real Satake parameter (Ciubotaru–Harris (6.4)); U₀^g ⊆ C_{0,h}. The hyperplanes ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ = 1, α^∨ ∈ Φ^{∨,+}, cut C₀ into m = ∏ᵢ (dᵢ + h)/dᵢ open regions (dᵢ the fundamental degrees of Φ^∨; 105 for F₄, 25 080 for E₈); an alcove is a connected component of the complement of all affine walls ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ℤ; U₀^g is a union of open regions intersected with C_{0,h}. Unitarity of L(s_c s_ν) for noncentral s_c is not governed by U₀^g (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: By spherical-generic-criterion and unramified-principal-series-irreducibility, ν ∈ C₀ gives a generic L(ν) iff ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ≠ 1 for all positive coroots.
Unitarity requires hermitian, so U₀^g ⊆ C_{0,h} (spherical-hermitian-criterion).
The count of regions is the classical count of the Shi-type arrangement in the dominant chamber, quoted by Ciubotaru–Harris.
acceptance: For PGL₂, U₀^g = {ν ∈ C₀ : ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ < 1} = A₀, the spherical complementary series; it has the single region below the wall.
0 ∈ U₀^g for every G.

sources.locator: §6, (6.4)–(6.6) and the paragraph between (6.5) and (6.6), pp. 17–18
sources.match: U₀^g is the set of dominant ν off the reducibility walls with L(ν) unitary; it lies in the hermitian locus and is a union of the open regions of the wall arrangement, whose number is ∏(dᵢ + h)/dᵢ.

uses.how: the set that is classified and intersected with the half-integral lattice
the zero complementary series CS(G(O^∨), 0) of the centraliser group is its U₀^g
