nodes.title: The fundamental alcove is unitary
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, A₀ ∩ C_{0,h} ⊆ U₀^g: for hermitian dominant ν with ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ < 1, L(ν) = X(ν) is generic and unitary (Ciubotaru–Harris Lemma 6.7).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: X(0) is unitarily induced and irreducible, hence unitary (SRU.2 unitary-induction, unramified-principal-series-irreducibility).

On the segment t ↦ tν, t ∈ [0, 1], every X(tν) is irreducible (⟨α^∨, tν⟩ ≤ ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ < 1 for positive coroots) and hermitian (w₀ν = −ν), with hermitian forms given by normalised long intertwining operators depending continuously on t.

The signature of a continuous family of nondegenerate hermitian forms on the K-types is constant (Knapp–Stein's complementary-series argument; the constancy of signature of the operators a_μ(χ) on facets, Barbasch–Ciubotaru §3.2), so X(ν) is unitary.
acceptance: For PGL₂ this is the classical complementary series 0 ≤ ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ < 1.
For PGL₃ (w₀ ≠ −1) only the hermitian ν = c(ω₁ + ω₂), 0 ≤ c < ½, of A₀ are covered.

sources.match: A₀ ∩ C_{0,h} ⊆ U₀^g by deforming from ν = 0 while X(ν) remains irreducible, the closest reducibility wall being ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ = 1 (citing Knapp–Stein).
For hermitian χ the positivity of the form is the positive semidefiniteness of the operators a_μ(χ), which have constant signature on each facet of the arrangement.

nodes.title: Unbounded regions are not unitary
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, if ν ∈ C₀ and ⟨αᵢ^∨, ν⟩ > 1 for some simple coroot αᵢ^∨, then ν ∉ U₀^g (Ciubotaru–Harris Lemma 6.8).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: Use signature constancy on the hermitian components of the complement of root-value-one hyperplanes. In the affine/graded Hecke algebra the normalised long intertwiner on the reflection W-type is indefinite on every unbounded region; see BCP §5.2, Lemma (2) and its following argument, p. 53.

In the dominant region with ⟨αᵢ^∨,ν⟩>1, move out along the fundamental-weight ray without crossing any root-value-one wall (all positive-coroot pairings are nondecreasing). In the hermitian locus use a ray invariant under −w₀, or its paired fundamental-weight ray. This places ν in an unbounded component, so it is not unitary. This is a signature argument, not a consequence of a single simple-root value forcing failure of coefficient decay.

The reflection-type signature calculation is a nonroutine classification input, included in the Hecke-signature gap below. BCP is stated for characteristic-zero groups; using it over function fields requires the characteristic-independent equal-parameter Hecke-algebra statement that CH26 uses.
acceptance: For PGL₂, ν with ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ > 1 gives X(ν) irreducible but not unitary: its spherical function grows or fails to decay.

sources.match: No unbounded region is unitary: ⟨αᵢ^∨, ν⟩ > 1 for a simple coroot excludes ν from U₀^g, citing Howe–Moore and Barbasch–Ciubotaru's spherical unitary principal series §3.3.
Only bounded regions contribute to the zero complementary series; the reflection W-type detects failure of positivity in unbounded regions.

nodes.title: Barbasch–Moy: unitarity through the Iwahori–Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let G be split over a nonarchimedean local field (characteristic zero is assumed by Barbasch–Moy and Barbasch–Ciubotaru; Ciubotaru–Harris §7 note the assumption is unnecessary for the Hecke-algebraic statements) and I an Iwahori subgroup. An irreducible representation π with π^I ≠ 0 is unitarizable iff the simple H(G, I)-module π^I is unitary for the *-structure f*(g) = conj f(g⁻¹) (Barbasch–Moy 1989); the Iwahori–Matsumoto involution preserves hermitian and unitary modules and exchanges spherical and generic ones; and the problem reduces to the graded affine Hecke algebra of the centraliser of s_c at the real infinitesimal character ν (Barbasch–Moy 1993).
hypotheses: G split; π irreducible Iwahori-spherical.
proofSteps: The Borel–Casselman equivalence V ↦ V^I (SR.3.4 borel-casselman-block) matches invariant hermitian forms on V with H(G, I)-invariant forms on V^I, the *-operation being adjoint for unitary structures (positive-definiteness on V reduces to V^I by e_I-averaging over K-types: Barbasch–Moy 1989).
The Iwahori–Matsumoto involution of H(G, I) (SR.1 iwahori-matsumoto) is a *-automorphism up to the sign twist, hence preserves unitarity; on the trivial character it gives the sign character.
The reduction to real infinitesimal character and to the graded algebra of Z_{G^∨}(s_c) is Lusztig's reduction made *-compatible by Barbasch–Moy; it is cited.
acceptance: The trivial and Steinberg representations correspond under the Iwahori–Matsumoto involution; both are unitary.
For non-real s_c the unitarity of L(s_c s_ν) is decided in the graded Hecke algebra of Z_{G^∨}(s_c), not of G^∨ (the source of PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11).

sources.match: The Iwahori–Matsumoto involution takes hermitian modules to hermitian ones and unitary to unitary, exchanging spherical and generic modules; by [BM1] the Iwahori-spherical unitary dual is equivalent to that of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra; by [BM2] it reduces to graded Hecke algebras of possibly smaller groups at real infinitesimal character.

sources.locator: D. Barbasch and A. Moy, A unitarity criterion for p-adic groups, Invent. Math. 98 (1989); Reduction to real infinitesimal character in affine Hecke algebras, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 6 (1993) (not read)
sources.match: The cited sources.

nodes.title: Classification of the generic unitary spherical dual
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, U₀^g is the intersection of C_{0,h} with a union of 2^d alcoves of C₀ including A₀, where d = 0 for PGL(n) and SO(2n+1), ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ for PSp(2n), n − 1 for PSO(4n) (n ≥ 2) and PSO(4n+2) (n ≥ 1), 1 for G₂, F₄, E₆, 3 for E₇ and 4 for E₈ (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 6.9, with the hermitian locus C_{0,h} in place of the printed C₀, PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E8). Explicitly (Barbasch–Ciubotaru §3.2–3.4): type A: ν = (ν₁, …, ν_k, (0,) −ν_k, …, −ν₁) with 0 ≤ ν₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ ν_k < ½; type C: 0 ≤ ν₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ νₙ < ½; types B, D: the alternating conditions of Barbasch–Ciubotaru Theorem 3.3; G₂: {3ν₁ + 2ν₂ < 1} ∪ {2ν₁ + ν₂ < 1 < 3ν₁ + ν₂}; F₄: {2ν₁ < 1} ∪ {ν₁ + ν₂ + ν₃ − ν₄ < 1 < ν₁ + ν₂ + ν₃ + ν₄}; E₆, E₇, E₈: the 2, 8 and 16 alcoves of Barbasch–Ciubotaru §7.2. The type-A case is part of Tadić's classification of the unitary dual of GL(n), owned upstream by AutomorphicSpectralTheory §7.0b.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: By barbasch-moy-unitarity the question is the unitarity of spherical modules of the graded Hecke algebra at real parameter ν.

The signature of the long intertwining operators on each W-type is constant on facets (fundamental-alcove-unitary, step 3); U₀^g is a union of regions, determined by checking finitely many W-types per region.

The case analysis is Barbasch (classical types), Ciubotaru (F₄, E₆) and Barbasch–Ciubotaru (E₇, E₈, and G₂, F₄ in their coordinates), and Tadić for GL(n); it is cited, and its decomposition into W-type signature computations is a remaining refinement of this layer.
acceptance: For PGL₂, d = 0 and U₀^g = A₀.
For G₂, d = 1: U₀^g has the fundamental alcove {3ν₁ + 2ν₂ < 1} and the second alcove {2ν₁ + ν₂ < 1 < 3ν₁ + ν₂} in Barbasch–Ciubotaru's coordinates.

sources.match: For quasi-simple split adjoint G, U₀^g is the hermitian locus intersected with a union of 2^d alcoves including A₀, with d listed by type; the classification is cited from [Ba, Ci1, Ci2, BC1] (the printed 'C₀' should be the hermitian locus, PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E8).
The 0-complementary series is listed type by type: the classical types after [BM3], [Ba1], G₂ and F₄ after [Ci1], and the 2, 8, 16 alcoves for E₆, E₇, E₈.

nodes.title: Nonzero integral root values are not unitary
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, if ν ∈ C₀ and ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ℤ_{>0} for some positive coroot α^∨, then ν ∉ U₀^g (Ciubotaru–Harris Proposition 6.10). Equivalently, for a real or central-compact s with α^∨(s) = q^m, m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, the generic L(s) is not unitary (Corollary 6.32(2), in that sector; sourceIssues E3).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
ν real (s_c = 1 or central).
proofSteps: A point with ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ = m ∈ ℤ_{>0} lies on an affine wall, hence in no open alcove; by generic-unitary-classification U₀^g is contained in a union of open alcoves intersected with C_{0,h}.
acceptance: For PGL₂, ν with ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ = 2 gives an irreducible non-unitary X(ν).

sources.locator: §6.1, Proposition 6.10 and proof, p. 18; Corollary 6.32(2) and proof, p. 25
sources.match: A dominant ν with a positive integral coroot value lies in no alcove and so is not in U₀^g; Corollary 6.32(2) is deduced from it.

nodes.title: Reduction of half-integral parameters
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, with 0 ≤ ε < ½: C₀^{½+ε} = ∅ unless ε ∈ {0, ¼}, and if G is quasi-simple of rank ≥ 2 then C₀^{½+ε} = ∅ unless ε = 0 ((6.12)). For ν = Σ νᵢωᵢ ∈ C₀^{½}, every νᵢ ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0}, and if moreover ν ∈ U₀^g then every νᵢ ∈ {0, ½} ((6.13)).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: Applying the condition to α^∨ and −α^∨ gives 2ε ∈ ½ℤ, so ε ∈ {0, ¼}.
In rank ≥ 2 take simple coroots α₁^∨, α₂^∨ with β^∨ = α₁^∨ + α₂^∨ a coroot: ⟨β^∨, ν⟩ ∈ 2ε + ½ℤ and ∈ ε + ½ℤ force ε ∈ ½ℤ, so ε = 0.
νᵢ = ⟨αᵢ^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0}; by unbounded-not-unitary νᵢ ≤ 1, and νᵢ = 1 is excluded by genericity (wall ⟨αᵢ^∨, ν⟩ = 1), leaving {0, ½}.
acceptance: For PGL₂ (rank one) ε = ¼ is possible: ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ = ¼ gives ⟨±α^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ¼ + ½ℤ; Ciubotaru–Harris use only ε = 0 there.

sources.match: ε must be 0 or ¼, and 0 in rank at least two using a sum of two simple coroots; half-integral dominant ν have νᵢ ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0}, and Lemma 6.8 cuts this to νᵢ ∈ {0, ½} for generic unitary ν.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for PGL(n)
nodes.statement: For G = PGL(n) in the setting of real-satake-parameter, write a dominant hermitian ν in standard coordinates as (a₁, …, a_k, −a_k, …, −a₁) for n = 2k and (a₁, …, a_k, 0, −a_k, …, −a₁) for n = 2k + 1, with a₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ a_k ≥ 0; the generic unitary region is 0 ≤ a_k ≤ ⋯ ≤ a₁ < ½ ((6.15), Tadić). Then U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ω_k} for n = 2k (the point a₁ = ⋯ = a_k = ¼) and U₀^{g,½} = {0} for n odd (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.3).
hypotheses: G = PGL(n), n ≥ 2; standard coordinates of Ciubotaru–Harris §6.3.
proofSteps: For n = 2k, ν is half-integral for the adjoint representation iff a_k ∈ ¼ℤ and the consecutive differences νᵢ − νᵢ₊₁ lie in ½ℤ; inside (6.15) this leaves a₁ = ⋯ = a_k ∈ {0, ¼}, i.e. ν ∈ {0, ½ω_k}, and ½ω_k satisfies (6.15).
For n odd, half-integrality forces every aᵢ ∈ ½ℤ, and (6.15) leaves only aᵢ = 0.
acceptance: For PGL₂ (k = 1), U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ω₁}, the complementary-series point with ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ = ½.
For PGL₃, U₀^{g,½} = {0}.

sources.match: In standard coordinates the unitary condition is 0 ≤ a_k ≤ ⋯ ≤ a₁ < ½ (citing Tadić); for n even the only nonzero half-integral point is ½ω_k with all aᵢ = ¼, and for n odd there is none.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for SO(2n+1)
nodes.statement: For G = SO(2n+1), with coroots α₁^∨ = 2ε₁, αᵢ^∨ = −εᵢ₋₁ + εᵢ (2 ≤ i ≤ n), weights ω₁ = ½(ε₁ + ⋯ + εₙ), ωᵢ = εᵢ + ⋯ + εₙ and highest coroot γ^∨ = 2εₙ (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.4): the only coroot of the maximal level r₀ = 2n − 1 is γ^∨ (Barbasch, Theorem 3.1), the unitary bound reads ν₁ + 2ν₂ + ⋯ + 2νₙ < 1, and U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ω₁}; ⟨γ^∨, ½ω₁⟩ = ½, so ½ω₁ lies in A₀.
hypotheses: G = SO(2n+1); coordinates of Ciubotaru–Harris §6.4.
proofSteps: By generic-unitary-classification every ν ∈ U₀^g has ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ < 1, i.e. ν₁ + 2ν₂ + ⋯ + 2νₙ < 1.
With νᵢ ∈ {0, ½} (half-integral-reduction) this forces ν₂ = ⋯ = νₙ = 0, leaving 0 and ½ω₁, and ½ω₁ ∈ A₀ is unitary (fundamental-alcove-unitary).
acceptance: For SO(3) ≅ PGL₂ (n = 1), the result agrees with half-integral-type-a: {0, ½ω₁}.

sources.match: For SO(2n+1) the level bound from Barbasch's Theorem 3.1 is ν₁ + 2ν₂ + ⋯ + 2νₙ < 1, leaving 0 and ½ω₁, which lies in the fundamental alcove.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for PSp(2n)
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 2, for G = PSp(2n), with coroots α₁^∨ = ε₁, αᵢ^∨ = −εᵢ₋₁ + εᵢ, weights ωᵢ = εᵢ + ⋯ + εₙ and highest coroot γ^∨ = εₙ₋₁ + εₙ (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.5): the maximal level is r₀ = n for n odd and n + 1 for n even, with the coroots (6.16), (6.17); the resulting bounds force ν₁ = ⋯ = ν_{⌊n/2⌋} = 0 and Σ_{j > ⌊n/2⌋} νⱼ < 1, leaving ½ωⱼ for j > ⌊n/2⌋, of which ½ωⱼ (j < n) lie on the wall ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ = 1. Hence U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ωₙ}, with ⟨γ^∨, ½ωₙ⟩ = ½.
hypotheses: G = PSp(2n); coordinates of Ciubotaru–Harris §6.5.
n ≥ 2 for the displayed ε_{n−1}+ε_n formula; the rank-one case PSp₂ = PGL₂ is handled by half-integral-type-a.
proofSteps: The coroots of level r₀ give the inequalities 2ν₁ + ν₂ + ⋯ < 1, …, displayed in §6.5 for n odd and even (generic-unitary-classification, after Barbasch Theorem 3.1).
With νᵢ ∈ {0, ½} (half-integral-reduction) they force ν₁ = ⋯ = ν_{⌊n/2⌋} = 0 and at most one νⱼ = ½ with j > ⌊n/2⌋.
For ⌊n/2⌋ < j < n, ⟨γ^∨, ½ωⱼ⟩ = 1, so ½ωⱼ is not generic; ½ωₙ ∈ A₀ is unitary (fundamental-alcove-unitary).
acceptance: For PSp(2) ≅ PGL₂, {0, ½ω₁} as in type A.
For PSp(4), the candidates ½ω₁ (excluded by ν₁ = 0) and ½ω₂ leave U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ω₂}.
For n=1 use PSp₂=PGL₂ and type A₁; do not interpret ε₀ in the rank ≥2 formula.

sources.match: For PSp(2n) the coroots of maximal level force the first ⌊n/2⌋ coordinates to vanish; of the remaining points ½ωⱼ only ½ωₙ avoids the wall γ^∨ = 1 and lies in the fundamental alcove.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for PSO(2n)
nodes.statement: For G = PSO(2n), with coroots α₁^∨ = ε₁ + ε₂, αᵢ^∨ = −εᵢ₋₁ + εᵢ, weights ω₁ = ½(ε₁ + ⋯ + εₙ), ω₂ = ½(−ε₁ + ε₂ + ⋯ + εₙ), ωᵢ = εᵢ + ⋯ + εₙ (i ≥ 3) and highest coroot γ^∨ = εₙ₋₁ + εₙ (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.6): for n even the maximal level is r₀ = n − 1 with the coroots (6.18), and U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ω₁, ½ω₂, ½ωₙ}; for n odd hermitian parameters need ν₁ = ν₂, which excludes ½ω₁ and ½ω₂, and U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ωₙ}. All listed nonzero points pair with γ^∨ to ½ and lie in A₀.
hypotheses: G = PSO(2n), n ≥ 3; coordinates of Ciubotaru–Harris §6.6.
proofSteps: For n even the level-r₀ coroots (6.18) force ν₃ = ⋯ = ν_{n/2} = 0 and at most one of ν₁, ν₂, νⱼ (j > n/2) equal to ½ (generic-unitary-classification, half-integral-reduction).
The points ½ωⱼ with n/2 < j < n lie on the wall ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ = 1; ½ω₁, ½ω₂, ½ωₙ pair with γ^∨ to ½ and lie in A₀, hence are unitary.
For n odd, w₀ν = −ν forces ν₁ = ν₂ (spherical-hermitian-criterion), excluding ½ω₁ and ½ω₂.
acceptance: For PSO(8) (n = 4) the three nonzero points ½ω₁, ½ω₂, ½ω₄ are permuted by triality.
For PSO(6) ≅ PGL₄ (n = 3), {0, ½ω₃} matches half-integral-type-a with k = 2 under the isomorphism.

sources.match: For PSO(2n), n even, the remaining nonzero points are ½ω₁, ½ω₂ and ½ωₙ in the fundamental alcove; for n odd ½ω₁ and ½ω₂ are not hermitian.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for G₂
nodes.statement: For G = G₂ in Bourbaki coordinates (6.19), the unique coroot of the maximal level r₀ = 3 is β^∨ = 2α₁^∨ + α₂^∨, giving the unitary bound 2ν₁ + ν₂ < 1 ((6.20)); hence ν₁ = 0, ν₂ ∈ {0, ½}, and ½ω₂ lies on the wall ⟨γ^∨, ν⟩ = 1 for the highest coroot γ^∨ = 3α₁^∨ + 2α₂^∨. So U₀^{g,½} = {0} (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.7).
hypotheses: G = G₂; coordinates (6.19).
proofSteps: The level bound is from Ciubotaru's classification (generic-unitary-classification, Ciubotaru F₄ paper Appendix B as cited).
2ν₁ < 1 with ν₁ ∈ ½ℤ gives ν₁ = 0; ν₂ < 1 gives ν₂ ∈ {0, ½}; ⟨3α₁^∨ + 2α₂^∨, ½ω₂⟩ = 1.
acceptance: ½ω₂ is the real part of the G₂ witness of g2-noncentral-witness, which is not generic for s_c = 1.

sources.match: In Bourbaki coordinates the only level-3 coroot gives 2ν₁ + ν₂ < 1; the remaining candidate ½ω₂ lies on the highest-coroot wall.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for F₄
nodes.statement: For G = F₄ in the coordinates (6.21), the unique coroot of the maximal level r₀ = 9 is β^∨ = (1, 1, 1, −1) = α₁^∨ + 2α₂^∨ + 4α₃^∨ + 2α₄^∨, giving ν₁ + 2ν₂ + 4ν₃ + 2ν₄ < 1 ((6.22)); hence ν₂ = ν₃ = ν₄ = 0, ν₁ ∈ {0, ½}, and ½ω₁ lies on the wall of the highest coroot γ^∨ = (2, 0, 0, 0). So U₀^{g,½} = {0} (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.8).
hypotheses: G = F₄; coordinates (6.21).
proofSteps: The level bound comes from Ciubotaru's F₄ table (generic-unitary-classification).
The inequality with νᵢ ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0} leaves ν = 0 or ½ω₁, and ⟨γ^∨, ½ω₁⟩ = 1.

sources.match: For F₄ the only level-9 coroot gives ν₁ + 2ν₂ + 4ν₃ + 2ν₄ < 1, leaving ½ω₁, which lies on the highest-coroot wall.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for E₆
nodes.statement: For G = E₆ in the coordinates (6.28), hermitian parameters satisfy ν₁ = ν₆ and ν₃ = ν₅; the unique coroot of the maximal level r₀ = 9 is β^∨ = α₁^∨ + α₂^∨ + 2α₃^∨ + 2α₄^∨ + 2α₅^∨ + α₆^∨ ((6.29)), giving 2ν₃ < 1, 2ν₄ < 1, 2ν₅ < 1 and ν₁ + ν₂ + ν₆ < 1; hence the only nonzero candidate is ½ω₂, which lies on the wall of the highest coroot. So U₀^{g,½} = {0} (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.11).
hypotheses: G = E₆; coordinates (6.28).
proofSteps: The level bound is from Ciubotaru's E₆ paper and Barbasch–Ciubotaru §7.2.1 (generic-unitary-classification).
ν₃ = ν₄ = ν₅ = 0; ν₁ = ν₆ with ν₁ + ν₂ + ν₆ < 1 forces ν₁ = ν₆ = 0; ½ω₂ pairs to 1 with γ^∨.
acceptance: The hermitian condition is needed: ½ω₁ alone satisfies the level bound but is not hermitian for E₆ (w₀ ≠ −1).

sources.match: For E₆, hermitian parameters have ν₁ = ν₆, ν₃ = ν₅; the level-9 coroot leaves only ½ω₂, which lies on the highest-coroot wall.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for E₇
nodes.statement: For G = E₇ in the coordinates (6.26), the coroots of the maximal level r₀ = 9 are the four listed in (6.27) (labels 46–49 of Barbasch–Ciubotaru), giving 2ν₃, 2ν₄, 2ν₅, 2ν₆ < 1 and ν₁ + ν₂ + ν₇ < 1; the candidates ½ω₁, ½ω₂ lie on the wall of the highest coroot γ^∨ = −ε₇ + ε₈, while ⟨γ^∨, ½ω₇⟩ = ½. So U₀^{g,½} = {0, ½ω₇} (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.10).
hypotheses: G = E₇; coordinates (6.26).
proofSteps: The level bound is from Barbasch–Ciubotaru §7.2.2 (generic-unitary-classification).
The inequalities leave ν₃ = ⋯ = ν₆ = 0 and at most one of ν₁, ν₂, ν₇ equal to ½.
½ω₁, ½ω₂ are on the wall γ^∨ = 1; ½ω₇ is in A₀, hence unitary (fundamental-alcove-unitary).
acceptance: ½ω₇ is the extra E₇ point that fundamental-separators removes using the 56-dimensional representation (pairing ¾).

sources.match: For E₇ the four level-9 coroots leave 0, ½ω₁, ½ω₂ and ½ω₇; the middle two lie on the highest-coroot wall and ½ω₇ lies in the fundamental alcove.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary points for E₈
nodes.statement: For G = E₈ in the coordinates (6.23)–(6.24), the coroots of the maximal level r₀ = 15 are the four listed in (6.25) (labels 89–92 of Barbasch–Ciubotaru), giving 2ν₂, 2ν₃, 4ν₄, 3ν₅, 2ν₆, 2ν₇ < 1 and ν₁ + ν₈ < 1; the candidates ½ω₁ and ½ω₈ lie on the wall of the highest coroot γ^∨ = ε₇ + ε₈. So U₀^{g,½} = {0} (Ciubotaru–Harris §6.9).
hypotheses: G = E₈; coordinates (6.23)–(6.24).
proofSteps: The level bound is from Barbasch–Ciubotaru §7.2.3 (generic-unitary-classification).
The inequalities leave ν₂ = ⋯ = ν₇ = 0 and ν₁, ν₈ ∈ {0, ½}, not both ½.
acceptance: In (6.24), ω₈ = ε₇ + ε₈, so ⟨ε₇ + ε₈, ½ω₈⟩ = 1.

sources.match: For E₈ the four level-15 coroots leave 0, ½ω₁ and ½ω₈, and the last two lie on the highest-coroot wall.

nodes.title: Half-integral generic unitary spherical parameters
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, U₀^{g,½} := U₀^g ∩ C₀^{½} is {0, ½ω_{n/2}} for PGL(n), n even, and {0} for n odd; {0, ½ω₁} for SO(2n+1); {0, ½ωₙ} for PSp(2n); {0, ½ω₁, ½ω₂, ½ωₙ} for PSO(2n), n even, and {0, ½ωₙ} for n odd; {0, ½ω₇} for E₇; {0} for G₂, F₄, E₆, E₈ (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 6.14, numbering of §§6.3–6.11); every nonzero element lies in the fundamental alcove A₀, and U₀^{g,½} = {0} unless G is of type A_{n−1} (n even), B, C, D or E₇.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
proofSteps: Assemble the nine type-by-type computations; the common strategy (Ciubotaru–Harris, proof of Theorem 6.14) is: the classification gives a maximal level r₀ ≥ 1 with ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ < 1 for all coroots of that level; the half-integral points satisfying these inequalities either lie on a reducibility wall (not generic) or are among the listed exceptions, all of which lie in A₀.
acceptance: For G₂, a generic unitary spherical L(ν) with real ν half-integral for the adjoint representation is tempered.

sources.match: The complete list of half-integral generic unitary real parameters of quasi-simple split adjoint groups.

nodes.title: Half-integrality is tested on the highest weight
nodes.statement: In the setting of half-integral-parameter, for ν ∈ C₀^{½} and V = V(λ^∨) irreducible of highest weight λ^∨, ν is half-integral for V iff ⟨λ^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ½ℤ (Ciubotaru–Harris Lemma 6.30).
hypotheses: ν ∈ C₀^{½}.
proofSteps: Every weight is λ^∨ − Σ aᵢ αᵢ^∨ with aᵢ ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, and ⟨αᵢ^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ½ℤ.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ and ν = ½ω₁ (⟨α^∨, ν⟩ = ½, so ν ∈ C₀^{½}), the highest weight ω₁^∨ = α^∨/2 of the standard representation of SL₂(ℂ) pairs to ¼ ∉ ½ℤ, so ν is not half-integral for it.

sources.match: For ν in C₀^{½}, half-integrality for V(λ^∨) is equivalent to ⟨λ^∨, ν⟩ ∈ ½ℤ, since weights differ from λ^∨ by integral combinations of simple roots.

nodes.title: Fundamental representations separate the extra half-integral points
nodes.statement: In the setting of half-integral-generic-unitary: ½ω_{n/2} is not half-integral for the defining representation V(ω₁^∨) of SL(n) (n even); ½ω₁ is not half-integral for the defining representation V(ωₙ^∨) of Sp(2n) (G = SO(2n+1)); ½ωₙ is not half-integral for the spin representation V(ω₁^∨) of Spin(2n+1) (G = PSp(2n)); for G = PSO(2n), ½ωₙ is not half-integral for the spin representation V(ω₁^∨) and ½ω₁, ½ω₂ are not for the defining representation V(ωₙ^∨); and ½ω₇ is not half-integral for the 56-dimensional V(ω₇^∨) of E₇ (Ciubotaru–Harris Proposition 6.31). The pairings are ¼ in the classical cases and ¾ for E₇. For type D both the spin and the defining representation are needed.
hypotheses: Numbering of Ciubotaru–Harris §§6.3–6.11.
proofSteps: By half-integrality-highest-weight it suffices to compute ⟨λ^∨, ν⟩ for the listed highest weights, which are ¼ (classical) and ¾ (E₇).
acceptance: For PGL₂ (n = 2), ⟨ω₁^∨, ½ω₁⟩ = ¼ for the standard representation of SL₂(ℂ).

sources.match: The extra points of Theorem 6.14 pair with the listed fundamental highest weights to ¼, or ¾ for E₇, and so are not half-integral for those representations.

nodes.title: The local generic temperedness test
nodes.statement: In the setting of real-satake-parameter, let s = s_c·s_ν with s_c = 1 or s_c central in G^∨ (the real or central-compact sector). If L(s) is generic and unitary, then s is geometric for the adjoint representation of G^∨ and for the fundamental representations of fundamental-separators iff ν = 0, i.e. iff L(s) = L(s_c) is tempered (Ciubotaru–Harris Corollary 6.32(1), corrected scope). As printed, for arbitrary s_c, the statement is false: see g2-noncentral-witness (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field of any characteristic with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) for 𝐆 quasi-simple, split and adjoint, K = 𝐆(O) hyperspecial, B ⊃ T a Borel subgroup and maximal split torus, based root datum (X, Φ, X^∨, Φ^∨, Π), Weyl group W, longest element w₀, Coxeter number h, dual group G^∨ over ℂ with maximal torus T^∨ = X ⊗ ℂ^× (Ciubotaru–Harris §6 setting).
s = s_c·s_ν with s_c = 1 or s_c central in G^∨ (the real or central-compact sector).
proofSteps: For central s_c, X(s_c s_ν) is the twist of X(s_ν) by the unitary character of G corresponding to s_c, so L(s) is generic unitary iff L(ν) is; WLOG ν dominant, so ν ∈ U₀^g.
Geometric for the adjoint representation means ν ∈ C₀^{½}, so ν ∈ U₀^{g,½} (half-integral-generic-unitary).

Every nonzero point of U₀^{g,½} fails half-integrality for a listed fundamental representation (fundamental-separators); hence ν = 0, and L(s) is tempered (spherical-tempered-criterion). The converse is immediate.
acceptance: For G = PGL₂ and s real with ν = ½ω₁ (a complementary-series point), the standard representation of SL₂(ℂ) detects non-geometricity.
The G₂ witness of g2-noncentral-witness lies outside the hypothesis (its s_c is not central).

sources.match: If the spherical L(s) is generic and unitary, geometricity for the adjoint and the listed fundamental representations holds iff ν = 0; the proof passes through ν ∈ U₀^g, valid only for real or central-compact s (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11).

nodes.title: The G₂ witness for noncentral compact parts
nodes.statement: Let G be split G₂ over k and s_c ∈ T^∨ the involution with (aα₁^∨ + bα₂^∨)(s_c) = (−1)^a (α₁^∨ the short simple coroot); its centraliser in G^∨ has type A₁ × Ã₁. For ν = ½ω₂ and s = s_c s_ν, X(s) is irreducible, L(s) = X(s) is generic and unitary, s is geometric for every representation of G^∨, and ν ≠ 0. Hence Corollary 6.32(1) fails for noncentral s_c, and the real part ½ω₂ is an extraneous point of CS(G₂, 0) (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11, E18).
hypotheses: G split G₂; s_c and ν as stated.
proofSteps: On the positive coroots (a, b) = (1,0), (0,1), (1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (3,2), α^∨(s) = −1, q^{1/2}, −q^{1/2}, q^{1/2}, −q^{1/2}, −q, never q^{±1}; the stabiliser W_s is trivial, so X(s) is irreducible (unramified-principal-series-irreducibility) and generic.

w₀ = −1 fixes s_c and negates ν, so X(s) is hermitian; along t ↦ s_c s_{tν}, t ∈ [0, 1], the same computation gives irreducibility, and at t = 0 the representation is unitarily induced, so X(s) is unitary (deformation as in fundamental-alcove-unitary).
Every weight of G₂(ℂ) lies in the root lattice and ν is half-integral for the adjoint representation, hence for all representations (half-integral-parameter, test halfIntegral_g2_all).
acceptance: L(s_ν) itself (real part only) is not generic: ⟨3α₁^∨ + 2α₂^∨, ν⟩ = 1, so ν ∉ U₀^g; the unitarity of L(s) is governed by the centraliser of s_c, not by U₀^g.

sources.match: The printed statement for arbitrary s = s_c s_ν; the witness is recorded as PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11 and its consequence for Theorem 8.5 as E18.

nodes.title: The τ-fixed dual group and the split group G(τ)
nodes.statement: Let k a nonarchimedean local field, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple of adjoint type, quasi-split and split over an unramified extension k'/k of degree d, not split; A a maximal split torus, M = Z_G(A), K a special maximal compact subgroup attached to A, B ⊃ A a Borel subgroup (Ciubotaru–Harris §7). The inner class of G gives a pinned automorphism τ of G^∨ of order d ∈ {2, 3}, normalised by τ(X_{α^∨}) = X_{τ(α^∨)} on root vectors. Unramified characters of M form the torus T'^∨ = Spec ℂ[Λ(M)] with X^*(T'^∨) = X^*(T^∨)^τ and W(G, A) = W^τ ((7.1)); the map η' : T^∨ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ → T'^∨, (s, τ) ↦ η(s), induces a bijection between τ-conjugacy classes of semisimple elements of G^∨ and W^τ-orbits in T'^∨ ((7.2)). X(s) = i_B(χ_s) and L(s) for s ∈ T'^∨ are as in SRU.5. G^∨(τ) := {g ∈ G^∨ : τ(g) = g} is connected reductive (G^∨ simply connected), and G(τ) is the split k-group with dual G^∨(τ): for the types ²A_{2n−1}, ²A_{2n}, ²D_n, ³D₄, ²E₆ of G, G(τ) has type B_n, C_n, C_{n−1}, G₂, F₄ respectively (Table 1). For real ν ∈ t'^∨_ℝ = (t^∨_ℝ)^τ write L^G(ν) and L^{G(τ)}(ν).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple of adjoint type, quasi-split and split over an unramified extension k'/k of degree d, not split; A a maximal split torus, M = Z_G(A), K a special maximal compact subgroup attached to A, B ⊃ A a Borel subgroup (Ciubotaru–Harris §7).
proofSteps: (7.1)–(7.2) are Borel's description of the unramified L-group parameters (Corvallis, §6, Lemma 6.4 and Proposition 6.7), which SR.4 frobenius-component-invariants and spherical-parameter state for unramified groups.

Connectedness of G^∨(τ): fixed points of a semisimple automorphism of a simply connected group are connected (Steinberg, Endomorphisms of linear algebraic groups, 8.1, cited); its type is read off from the folded Dynkin diagram, giving Table 1.
acceptance: For G = PSU(2, 2) (²A₃), G^∨ = SL₄(ℂ), G^∨(τ) = Sp₄(ℂ) and G(τ) = SO₅, of type B₂.
For G = PSU(3) (²A₂), G^∨(τ) = SO₃(ℂ) and G(τ) = Sp₂ = SL₂, of type C₁.

sources.match: For quasi-split unramified adjoint G the pinned τ, the identification of unramified characters with T'^∨ and of W(G, A) with W^τ, the bijection of τ-conjugacy classes with W^τ-orbits, the fixed group G^∨(τ) and the split group G(τ) with Table 1 of types.
The graded Hecke algebra of G at s_e is identified with that of the split group whose dual is G(s_e τ).

uses.how: the comparison group G(τ) to which the split results of §6 are applied
places where G is unramified and quasi-split but not split

nodes.title: Unitary transfer from nonsplit unramified to split groups
nodes.statement: In the setting of tau-fixed-dual-group, for every real ν ∈ t'^∨_ℝ, L^G(ν) is unitary iff L^{G(τ)}(ν) is unitary, and generic unitary iff L^{G(τ)}(ν) is generic unitary (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 7.4, a case of Barbasch–Ciubotaru 2013 Corollary 6.2.6). Barbasch–Ciubotaru assume characteristic zero (§1.3); Ciubotaru–Harris note that the assumption is unnecessary, the statement being one about graded Hecke algebras.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple of adjoint type, quasi-split and split over an unramified extension k'/k of degree d, not split; A a maximal split torus, M = Z_G(A), K a special maximal compact subgroup attached to A, B ⊃ A a Borel subgroup (Ciubotaru–Harris §7).
ν real.
proofSteps: BC3 Theorem 1.3.1 and Theorem 1.4.1, pp. 3–4, give the unitary categorical comparison for unramified groups with the fixed root datum. This is the nonsplit theorem; SRU.5’s split-only Barbasch–Moy statement alone does not justify this step.

BC3 Corollary 6.2.6 and Example 6.2.7, p. 29, identify the companion at compact part one, with its actual isogeny. Keep Sp(2n) for the odd unitary group. The comparison for arbitrary compact part uses Z_{G^∨}(s_cτ), which can be disconnected.

The genericity assertion is CH26 Theorem 7.4, pp. 25–26. Its proof needs the transport of the nonsplit Whittaker/sign criterion through the Hecke equivalence. This adapter and the passage from the characteristic-zero group theorem to characteristic-independent Hecke algebras are explicitly recorded in the Hecke-signature/transfer gap.
acceptance: For ν = 0 both sides are unitary principal series and the statement is immediate.
For G = PSU(2,2) the generic unitary real spherical parameters are those of SO₅ (type B₂) in SRU.5 generic-unitary-classification.

sources.match: For real ν in the τ-fixed space, L^G(ν) is (generic) unitary iff L^{G(τ)}(ν) is, a particular case of [BC3, Corollary 6.2.6]; the characteristic-zero assumption of [BC3] is unnecessary.

Barbasch–Ciubotaru work over p-adic fields of characteristic zero and prove that the real-infinitesimal-character categories of G and of G(s_e τ) are unitarily equivalent, in particular for Iwahori-fixed vectors between G and G(τ).

sources.locator: §1.3, Theorem 1.3.1; §1.4, Theorem 1.4.1, pp. 3–4; §6.2, Corollary 6.2.6 and Example 6.2.7, p. 29
sources.match: Unitary equivalences retain arbitrary isogeny and the compact-part twisted centraliser; at compact part one they give the split companions with their actual root data.

nodes.title: The generic temperedness test for nonsplit unramified groups
nodes.statement: In the setting of tau-fixed-dual-group, assume G is not the quasi-split form of PSU(2n+1), and let s = s_c s_ν ∈ T'^∨ with s_c = 1 or central. If L^G(s) is generic and unitary, then s is geometric with respect to all finite-dimensional representations of G^∨ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ iff ν = 0, i.e. iff L^G(s) = L^G(s_c) is tempered (Ciubotaru–Harris Corollary 7.5, scope corrected as in SRU.5 generic-temperedness-test; PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E11). The representations used are the adjoint representation (τ-stable, whose restriction contains the adjoint representation of G^∨(τ)), V ⊕ V^τ for G^∨ = SL(2n) (restricting to two copies of the defining representation of Sp(2n)), and the sum of the two half-spin representations for G^∨ = Spin(2n) (restricting to two copies of the spin representation of Spin(2n−1)).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple of adjoint type, quasi-split and split over an unramified extension k'/k of degree d, not split; A a maximal split torus, M = Z_G(A), K a special maximal compact subgroup attached to A, B ⊃ A a Borel subgroup (Ciubotaru–Harris §7).
G not the quasi-split PSU(2n+1)
s_c = 1 or central.

A compact part called central means central in the full L-dual group and compatible with a unitary unramified character twist; being central merely in the abelian parameter torus is insufficient. Otherwise keep the compact part equal to one.
proofSteps: By nonsplit-unitary-transfer, L^{G(τ)}(ν) is generic unitary.

Restrictions to G^∨(τ) of the listed representations of G^∨ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ contain the adjoint representation of G^∨(τ) and the fundamental representations of SRU.5 fundamental-separators for the type of G(τ); for the exceptional G(τ) (G₂, F₄) the adjoint representation suffices since U₀^{g,½} = {0}.
SRU.5 generic-temperedness-test applied to G(τ) gives ν = 0.
acceptance: For G of type ²E₆, G(τ) = F₄ and the adjoint representation alone forces ν = 0.
For the quasi-split PSU(2n+1) the argument fails (odd-unitary-residual).

sources.match: For nonsplit unramified adjoint G other than the quasi-split PSU(2n+1), generic unitary L^G(s) is geometric for all representations of G^∨ ⋊ ⟨τ⟩ iff ν = 0; the proof restricts V ⊕ V^τ and the half-spin representations to G^∨(τ) and applies Proposition 6.31; it passes from L^G(s) to L^G(ν) as in Corollary 6.32, so the same restriction on s_c applies.

nodes.title: The residual candidate for the odd quasi-split unitary group
nodes.statement: Let G be the quasi-split form of PSU(2n+1): G^∨ = SL(2n+1, ℂ), G^∨(τ) = SO(2n+1, ℂ), G(τ) = Sp(2n). Assume L^G(ν) is generic and unitary, ν is real, and the geometric half-integrality test holds for every finite-dimensional representation of the ambient dual SL(2n+1,ℂ). Under these hypotheses, the argument of nonsplit-generic-temperedness leaves the two possibilities ν = 0 and ν = ½ωₙ (the G(τ)-weight in the numbering of Ciubotaru–Harris §6.5): the adjoint representation of G^∨ restricts to contain the adjoint representation of G^∨(τ), which leaves {0, ½ωₙ} (SRU.5 half-integral-type-c for PSp(2n)), and ½ωₙ is excluded for PSp(2n) only by the spin representation of Spin(2n+1, ℂ), which does not factor through SO(2n+1, ℂ) and so does not occur in any representation of SL(2n+1, ℂ) (Ciubotaru–Harris Remark 7.6). This is not an automorphic counterexample.
hypotheses: G the quasi-split adjoint unitary group in 2n + 1 variables over k.
L^G(ν) generic unitary, ν real, and the half-integrality condition holds in every finite-dimensional ambient-dual representation; the Sp/PSp comparison requires the adapter in the transfer gap.
proofSteps: nonsplit-unitary-transfer and SRU.5 half-integral-type-c for PSp(2n) give ν ∈ {0, ½ωₙ}.
Representations of SL(2n+1, ℂ) restrict to SO(2n+1, ℂ), on which the centre of Spin(2n+1, ℂ) acts trivially; the spin representation is faithful on that centre, so it is not a constituent.
acceptance: For n = 1 (PSU(3)), G(τ) = SL₂ and the residual candidate is ½ω₁, the half-integral complementary-series point of SL₂.

sources.match: For the quasi-split PSU(2n+1) the methods leave ν = 0 or ν = ½ωₙ; the spin representation that rules out ½ωₙ for PSp(2n) does not descend to SO(2n+1, ℂ).

nodes.title: The Aubert–Zelevinsky involution
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(F) be reductive over a nonarchimedean local field with minimal parabolic B and simple roots Δ, and R(G) the Grothendieck group of finite-length smooth complex representations. D_G := Σ_{J⊆Δ} (−1)^{|J|} i_{P_J} ∘ r_{P_J} on R(G), with normalised induction and Jacquet functors of the standard parabolics P_J (Aubert Définition 1.5). D_G commutes with the contragredient, satisfies D_G ∘ i_{P_J} = i_{P_J} ∘ D_{L_J} and r_{P_J} ∘ D_G = Ad(w_J) ∘ D_{L_{J'}} ∘ r_{P_{J'}} for the conjugate subset J' = w_J(J) (Théorème 1.7(1)–(2)), is an involution, D_G² = id (1.7(3)), and acts on an irreducible cuspidal π by (−1)^{|Δ|} (1.7(4)). For irreducible π, ±D_G(π) is irreducible for a unique sign (Corollaire 3.9); AZ(π) denotes this irreducible representation. AZ preserves cuspidal support, AZ(1_G) = St_G for split G, and for GL_n it is Zelevinsky's involution (Théorème 2.3), the involution of SR.5.3. The characteristic-zero endpoint is independently corroborated by Ban02 Theorem 3.1. Ciubotaru–Harris use the same involution over function fields; checking the corrected-resolution proof and its characteristic extension remains the explicit Aubert gap below.
hypotheses: G reductive over a nonarchimedean local field; representations of finite length.
proofSteps: D_G is additive and well defined on R(G): i_P is exact and preserves finite length (SR.2 parabolic-induction; SR.3 finite-length (1)); r_P is exact over ℂ (SR.2 jacquet-lemma), takes admissible to admissible (SR.2 jacquet-invariants) and finitely generated to finitely generated (SR.2 jacquet-module), hence finite length to finite length (SR.3 finite-length (2)).

Théorème 1.7(2) is the geometric lemma (SR.2 geometric-lemma) summed with signs over the subsets J; (3) follows from (2) by induction on the semisimple rank and (4) for cuspidals; (1) uses Casselman's duality of r_P with the contragredient.

Irreducibility up to sign is the endpoint cited in Aubert Corollaire 3.9 and independently restated in Ban02 Theorem 3.1(6), p. 678, whose reference includes Aubert’s 1996 erratum. The original resolution proof and the correction were not accessible for this independent review, so their proof input is recorded as a gap rather than declared exact from the uncorrected 1995 paper.
Cuspidal support: every term i_{P_J} ∘ r_{P_J}(π) has the cuspidal support of π (SR.3 cuspidal-support).

AZ(1) = St for split G: by Théorème 1.7(2) with J = ∅, r_B(D_G[1]) = ±Ad(w₀)(r_B 1) = ±δ_B^{1/2}, a single exponent; among the constituents of i_B(δ_B^{1/2}) only St_G has normalised Jacquet module δ_B^{1/2} (SR.3.4 steinberg; SRU.4 rodier-steinberg-series), so AZ(1) = St_G.
acceptance: For GL₂(ℚ_p): AZ(1) = St, AZ(St) = 1, and AZ fixes every irreducible principal series and every supercuspidal.
D_G² = id on R(G).

sources.match: D_G is the alternating sum over standard Levi subgroups of induction composed with the Jacquet functor; it commutes with the contragredient, is compatible with induction and Jacquet functors, is an involution and multiplies irreducible cuspidals by (−1)^{|S|}.
For GL_n the involution coincides with Zelevinsky's; for irreducible E, ±D_G(E) is the class of an irreducible representation E^#, and (E^#)^# ≅ E.
For tempered π, π and AZ(π) have the same cuspidal support, by [Au, Theorem 1.7].

The alternating induction–Jacquet operator is involutive, compatible with induction and Jacquet functors, and takes irreducibles to irreducibles up to sign; the cited Aubert reference includes the 1996 erratum.

AZ(L(s)) = π(s, e, triv) with e in the open orbit defines the nilpotent stratum of a spherical representation
the spherical representation at the central point is the AZ dual of a tempered one

nodes.title: Aubert duality preserves the semisimple parameter
nodes.statement: Let G be connected reductive over a nonarchimedean local field and π irreducible (Ciubotaru–Harris state it for tempered π). Then π and AZ(π) are constituents of the same normalised parabolically induced representation of a cuspidal datum; hence their semisimple local parameters (ExcursionOperators ES5) coincide: L^ss(AZ(π)) = L^ss(π) (Ciubotaru–Harris Proposition 4.5). No equality of monodromy operators is asserted.
hypotheses: π irreducible; the semisimple parameter L^ss of ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES5, compatible with parabolic induction (ES7:parabolic).
A fixed field isomorphism ℂ ≅ Q̄_ℓ (ℓ ≠ p), through which complex representations are compared with the ℓ-adic coefficients of ES5.
proofSteps: Same cuspidal support: aubert-involution.

The semisimple parameter of an irreducible constituent of i_P(σ) is that of σ composed with the Levi embedding (ExcursionOperators ES7:parabolic parabolic-induction), with the half-modulus twist of normalised induction accounted for by ES7:parabolic normalised-induction-dictionary; it depends only on the cuspidal support.
acceptance: For GL₂, L^ss(1) = L^ss(St) = |·|^{1/2} ⊕ |·|^{−1/2}, while the Weil–Deligne monodromies differ (0 and nonzero).

sources.match: For tempered π, π and AZ(π) are constituents of the same normalised induced representation, so their semisimple ℓ-adic parameters agree; the proof cites [Au, Theorem 1.7].

nodes.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig parameters
nodes.statement: Let k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple, adjoint and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting). A Kazhdan–Lusztig triple is (s, e, ρ) with s ∈ G^∨ semisimple, e ∈ g^∨ nilpotent with Ad(s)e = q·e, and ρ an irreducible representation of the component group A(s, e) = π₀(Z_{G^∨}(s, e)) of Springer type (occurring in the homology of the variety of Borel subalgebras containing e and fixed by s), on which the centre of G^∨ acts trivially; triples are taken up to G^∨-conjugacy. g^∨_q denotes the q-eigenspace of Ad(s); G^∨(s) = Z_{G^∨}(s) acts on it with finitely many orbits and a unique open orbit. For a Lie triple (e, h, f) with h ∈ t^∨_ℝ and s ∈ T^∨, s₀ := s q^{−h/2} commutes with the triple.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple, adjoint and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
For connected-centre G the classification is Kazhdan–Lusztig's; general isogeny is Reeder's.
proofSteps: Finiteness of G^∨(s)-orbits on g^∨_q and the open orbit are the graded (Vinberg–Lusztig) version of finiteness of nilpotent orbits.

The Springer-type condition uses the Springer correspondence on the component groups; it is a definition here, with the geometric inputs (nilpotent orbits, sl₂-triples, Springer fibres) recorded as gaps (nilpotent-orbit owner pending).
acceptance: For PGL₂: triples (s, 0, triv) for all s, and (s, e ≠ 0, triv) for s with eigenvalue ratio q, the latter giving the Steinberg representation and its unramified quadratic twist.
The spherical triples are exactly those with e = 0 and ρ trivial.

sources.match: Irreducible Iwahori-spherical representations correspond to G^∨-conjugacy classes of triples (s, e^∨, ρ) with Ad(s)e^∨ = qe^∨ and ρ of Springer type; spherical, tempered and generic representations are described in these terms.

sources.locator: D. Kazhdan and G. Lusztig, Proof of the Deligne–Langlands conjecture for Hecke algebras, Invent. Math. 87 (1987), Theorem 7.12; M. Reeder, Represent. Theory 6 (2002), Theorem 1 (not read)
sources.match: The classification for connected centre and for general isogeny.

uses.how: spherical, generic and AZ-dual representations are described by their KL triples
tempered spherical representations are the full principal series

api.name: KLTriple.conj

nodes.title: The Kazhdan–Lusztig classification of Iwahori-spherical representations
nodes.statement: Let k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple, adjoint and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting). Irreducible smooth representations of G with nonzero Iwahori-fixed vectors are in bijection, π(s, e, ρ) ↔ (s, e, ρ), with G^∨-conjugacy classes of Kazhdan–Lusztig triples (Kazhdan–Lusztig 1987 Theorem 7.12 for connected centre; Reeder 2002 in general). Moreover: (1) π(s, e, ρ) is K-spherical iff e = 0, and then ρ is trivial and π(s, 0, triv) = L(s) with s the Satake parameter; (2) π(s, e, ρ) is tempered iff s₀ is compact; (3) π(s, e, ρ) is generic iff ρ is trivial and e lies in the open G^∨(s)-orbit of g^∨_q; (4) AZ(L(s)) = π(s, e, triv) with e in that open orbit (Ciubotaru–Harris §5 and §8.1).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple, adjoint and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
proofSteps: The Iwahori block is equivalent to H(G, I)-modules (SR.3.4 borel-casselman-block), and H(G, I) is the affine Hecke algebra with Bernstein presentation (SR.1).

Kazhdan–Lusztig realise H(G, I) in the equivariant K-theory of the Steinberg variety of G^∨ and classify simple modules by standard modules in the homology of fixed-point varieties; this geometric proof is not decomposed here (gaps: equivariant K-theory realisation).

(1) Spherical modules contain the trivial H(K, I)-character, which occurs exactly for e = 0; (2) Casselman's criterion in terms of the exponents of the standard module; (3) Barbasch–Moy, Reeder; (4) on Iwahori-spherical modules the Aubert involution is the Iwahori–Matsumoto involution (az-iwahori-matsumoto), which exchanges spherical and generic modules with the same s.

The adjoint hypothesis is essential to the simplified spherical criterion as written. With arbitrary isogeny e=0 need not force the component-group representation to be trivial. A general dictionary must impose e=0 and trivial enhancement, and keep the Whittaker datum in the generic criterion; that extension is not claimed here.
acceptance: For PGL₂: L(s) = π(s, 0, triv); St = π(diag(q^{1/2}, q^{−1/2}), e, triv); at s = diag(q^{1/2}, q^{−1/2}) the q-eigenspace is the line of e, the open orbit is e ≠ 0, so AZ(1) = St.
Tempered spherical representations have s₀ = s compact and g^∨_q = 0, so they are the only irreducible representations with that s (Ciubotaru–Harris, proof of Corollary 5.7).

sources.match: The KL classification, its spherical and tempered criteria, the description of generic representations by the open orbit in the q-eigenspace, and AZ(L(s)) = π(s, e^∨, triv) with e^∨ in that orbit.
The cited classification.

nodes.title: Aubert duality on the Iwahori block preserves unitarity
nodes.statement: Let k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting). On irreducible Iwahori-spherical representations, AZ corresponds under V ↦ V^I to the central-character-preserving Iwahori–Matsumoto involution of H(G, I) specified below, which preserves hermitian and unitary modules. Hence AZ(π) is unitarizable iff π is, for Iwahori-spherical π; in particular AZ of a tempered Iwahori-spherical representation is unitarizable.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
proofSteps: Fix the central-character-preserving convention of La24 Definition 4.2, p. 18, in Bernstein generators: IM(T_s)=−qT_s⁻¹ for finite simple reflections, and IM(θ_x)=T_{w₀} θ_{w₀x} T_{w₀}⁻¹. It fixes the Bernstein centre. The other common convention with θ_x↦θ_{−x} has a different effect on central characters and must not be substituted here.

Kato’s alternating induction–restriction identity identifies this involution with D_G on the Iwahori block, using compatibility of Iwahori invariants with normalised induction and Jacquet restriction (La24 Theorem 4.3, p. 18). Agreement on 1 and St and induction compatibility alone would not prove equality of functors.

For the graded convention tw↦(−1)^ℓ(w)tw and ω↦−ω, unitarity is preserved (CiF4 Theorem 3.1, pp. 10–11 of the author version). Passing to the central-character-preserving version composes with the opposition automorphism/inner conjugacy, which preserves positive forms; retain this convention adapter through the affine-to-graded equivalence.
SRU.5 barbasch-moy-unitarity: the Iwahori–Matsumoto involution preserves unitary H(G, I)-modules (Barbasch–Ciubotaru §1.1, after [BM1]).
Tempered representations are unitarizable (SR.3.3 and SRU.2 unitary-induction).
acceptance: AZ(St) = 1 is unitary.
For PGL₂ the complementary series L(ν), 0 < ⟨α^∨, ν⟩ < 1, are fixed by AZ (they are full principal series) and unitary.

sources.match: The Iwahori–Matsumoto involution takes hermitian modules to hermitian modules and unitary to unitary, interchanging spherical and generic modules and the trivial and Steinberg representations ([BM1]).
The spherical representation at the central point is the AZ dual of a tempered representation and is unitary.

The central-character-preserving involution has an explicit Bernstein-generator formula and equals the alternating induction–restriction operator; the alternative inverse-torus convention is distinguished.

sources.locator: §3.1, Theorem 3.1, pp. 10–11 of the author version
sources.match: The usual graded Iwahori–Matsumoto involution preserves unitarity; the central-point spherical module is its dual of a tempered module.

nodes.title: The nilpotent partition of the spherical dual
nodes.statement: Let k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple, adjoint and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting). For a nilpotent G^∨-orbit O^∨ ⊆ g^∨, Sph(G, O^∨) is the set of G^∨-classes of s with AZ(L(s)) = π(s, e, triv), e ∈ O^∨ ((8.1)); these sets partition the K-spherical dual. For a Lie triple (e^∨, h^∨, f^∨) of O^∨, s = q^{h^∨/2} ∈ Sph(G, O^∨) is the central point. For s ∈ T^∨ write s = q^{ℜ(s)} s_c with ℜ(s) ∈ t^∨_ℝ and Sph(G, O^∨)₀ for the set of real parts. SU(G) is the spherical unitary dual (s with L(s) unitarizable), CS(G, O^∨) = SU(G) ∩ Sph(G, O^∨) the spherical complementary series attached to O^∨, and CS(G, O^∨)₀ its real parts; SU(G) = ⊔ CS(G, O^∨). Z(O^∨) = C_{G^∨}(e^∨, h^∨, f^∨) is reductive, possibly disconnected, with Lie algebra z(O^∨); G(O^∨) is the split group dual to Z(O^∨)°; choosing a Cartan subalgebra a^∨ ⊆ z(O^∨) inside t^∨, for s with trivial or central compact part, ℜ(s) ∈ Sph(G, O^∨)₀ can be written ℜ(s) = ½h^∨ + ν with ν ∈ a^∨_ℝ, regarded as a parameter in Sph(G(O^∨), 0)₀ ((8.2)).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple, adjoint and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
proofSteps: The partition: each L(s) has exactly one AZ dual, whose KL triple has e in the open orbit of g^∨_q (kazhdan-lusztig-classification (4)); its G^∨-saturation is O^∨.
Central point: for s = q^{h^∨/2}, Ad(s)e^∨ = qe^∨ and the triple has s₀ = 1 compact, so π(s, e^∨, triv) is tempered and L(s) is its AZ dual (Barbasch–Ciubotaru §1.3, (1.3.1)).

The decomposition ℜ(s) = ½h^∨ + ν with ν in the centraliser follows from Barbasch–Moy's characterisation of O(χ) (Barbasch–Ciubotaru §1.3, (1.3.1)–(1.3.2)); the existence of Lie triples and the reductivity of Z(O^∨) are nilpotent-orbit inputs (gaps: nilpotent-orbit owner pending).
acceptance: For O^∨=0, the real slice {ν | q^ν∈CS(G,0)} equals U₀^g up to W. This does not identify all real parts CS(G,0)₀ when arbitrary compact parts are allowed.
For regular O^∨ the real slice is {q^ρ}; the full stratum also contains central compact twists zq^ρ. For PGL₂ the two choices of z give the trivial and unramified quadratic characters.

sources.match: The sets Sph(G, O^∨), the central point q^{h^∨/2}, the real parts, the spherical unitary dual SU(G), the complementary series CS(G, O^∨), the centraliser Z(O^∨) and the split group G(O^∨), and the decomposition ℜ(s) = ½h^∨ + ν.
Barbasch–Moy attach to each real χ a unique maximal nilpotent orbit O(χ) with wχ = ½h + ν, ν in the centraliser, equivalently the saturation of the open G₀-orbit in g₁.

uses.how: the stratification in which complementary series and extraneous points are classified
the global weight-pattern argument places all unramified components in the same CS(G, O^∨)

nodes.title: The central point is unitary
nodes.statement: In the setting of nilpotent-partition, for every nilpotent O^∨ the spherical representation L(q^{h^∨/2}) at the central point is unitarizable (Ciubotaru–Harris §8.1).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple, adjoint and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
proofSteps: L(q^{h^∨/2}) = AZ(π(q^{h^∨/2}, e^∨, triv)) with the second tempered (nilpotent-partition, step 2).
az-iwahori-matsumoto: the AZ dual of a tempered Iwahori-spherical representation is unitarizable.
acceptance: For O^∨ regular the central point is the trivial representation; for O^∨ = 0 it is X(1), a unitary principal series.

sources.match: The spherical representation at the central point q^{h/2} is the AZ dual of a tempered representation and is unitary.

nodes.title: Complementary series reduce to the triple centraliser
nodes.statement: In the setting of nilpotent-partition, with G of connected centre or adjoint as in Ciubotaru–Harris §8: assuming s has trivial or central compact part, if O^∨ is not the orbit 4A₁ of E₈, s ∈ CS(G, O^∨) and ℜ(s) = ½h^∨ + ν with ν ∈ Sph(G(O^∨), 0)₀, then ν ∈ CS(G(O^∨), 0)₀ (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 8.3). For 4A₁ in E₈ the complementary series has an extra region beyond that of the centraliser C₄ (e8-4a1-exclusion).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
O^∨ ≠ 4A₁ ⊂ E₈.

s=q^{ℜ(s)} or s=zq^{ℜ(s)} with z compact and central in the full dual group; strip the corresponding unitary unramified character twist first. No assertion here covers arbitrary noncentral compact part.
proofSteps: Strip a central compact part using its unitary unramified character twist (with the full root datum retained). For the remaining real parameter, use the real graded-Hecke equivalence. For noncentral compact part the relevant graded root system is that of Z_{G^∨}(s_c), so replacing it by G^∨ at ℜ(s) would be invalid.

The classification of the spherical unitary dual (Barbasch for classical types, Ciubotaru for F₄ and E₆, Barbasch–Ciubotaru for E₇, E₈) shows, case by case, that the ν occurring are in the zero complementary series of G(O^∨), except for 4A₁ in E₈; the case analysis is cited.
acceptance: For O^∨ = 0, G(O^∨) = G and the statement is the definition of U₀^g.
For O^∨ regular, Z(O^∨) is the centre, G(O^∨) is trivial and ν = 0.

sources.match: Except for 4A₁ in E₈, a complementary-series parameter ½h^∨ + ν attached to O^∨ has ν in the zero complementary series of the centraliser group, by the classification of the spherical unitary dual [Ba, BC1, Ci1, Ci2].

nodes.title: Extraneous real parts
nodes.statement: In the setting of nilpotent-partition, let s = φ(Frob) ∈ CS(G, O^∨) be geometric in the sense of SRU.5 half-integral-parameter (for every representation of G^∨). Its real part ℜ(s) is extraneous if it is not W-conjugate to the central point ½h^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris Definition 8.4).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
proofSteps: Well defined: ℜ(s) is defined up to W, and the central point of O^∨ up to W.
acceptance: The central point itself is never extraneous.
For Sp(6) and O^∨ = (2,2,2), ½h^∨ = (½, ½, ½) and the point (0, ½, 1) is extraneous (Remark 8.6).

sources.match: When s is geometric and L(s) unitary but its real part is not the central point, the real part is called extraneous; the smallest example is in Sp(6) at the orbit (2,2,2).

nodes.title: Extraneous points for symplectic and spin duals
nodes.statement: In the setting of extraneous-point, with G of connected centre and s = s_c q^ν with s_c = 1 or s_c central in G^∨: (1) if G^∨ = Sp(2n) and O^∨ has partition with rᵢ parts equal to i (Σ i rᵢ = 2n, rᵢ even for i odd), so that Z(O^∨) = ∏_{i odd} Sp(rᵢ) × ∏_{j even} O(rⱼ), the extraneous real parts are ½h^∨ + ½ Σ_{j even, rⱼ ≥ 3} εⱼ ω^j_{⌊rⱼ/2⌋}, εⱼ ∈ {0, 1} not all zero; (2) if G^∨ = Spin(n) and O^∨ has rᵢ parts equal to i (Σ i rᵢ = n, rᵢ even for i even), the extraneous real parts are ½h^∨ + ½ Σ_{i odd, rᵢ ≥ 3} εᵢ ω^i_{⌊rᵢ/2⌋} with Σ εᵢ even and not all εᵢ zero (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 8.5(1)–(2); the proof's 'j odd' in case (2) of Sp is a misprint for 'j even', PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E2). These lists are not asserted for noncentral compact parts.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
G of connected centre
s = s_c q^ν with s_c = 1 or s_c central in G^∨.
proofSteps: Write ℜ(s) = ½h^∨ + ν with ν ∈ CS(G(O^∨), 0)₀ (centralizer-reduction). ½h^∨ is half-integral for every representation (sl₂-theory), so ν is half-integral for every representation of g^∨ and for the adjoint representation of z(O^∨).
Apply SRU.5 half-integral-generic-unitary to each simple factor of z(O^∨): ν is 0 or an exception of Theorem 6.14 on each factor.

Standard representation of G^∨: forces νᵢ = 0 on the factors that are not of the listed orthogonal type; for Spin(n) the spin modules impose the parity Σ εᵢ even; the remaining points are half-integral for G^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris, proof of Theorem 8.5, cases (2)–(3)).
acceptance: Remark 8.6: for Sp(6) and O^∨ = (2,2,2) (r₂ = 3), the unique extraneous real part is ½h^∨ + ½ω^2_1 = (0, ½, 1) up to W.
For O^∨ with every rⱼ ≤ 2 (j even), there are no extraneous points.

sources.locator: §8.2, Theorem 8.5(1)–(2), Remark 8.6 and proof cases (1)–(3), pp. 28–29

nodes.title: Extraneous points for exceptional duals
nodes.statement: In the setting of extraneous-point, with G of connected centre and s = s_c q^ν with s_c = 1 or s_c central in G^∨: the extraneous real parts occur only for O^∨ = B₃ (real part ω₁ + ½ω₃ + ½ω₄, corrected from the printed ω₁ + ω₂ + ½ω₃ + ½ω₄, PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E5) and Ã₁ + A₁ (½ω₁ + ½ω₄) in F₄; D₅(a₁) + A₁ in E₇ (½(ω₁ + ω₂ + ω₃ + ω₆ + ω₇)); and the following four E₈ points: D₆ (centraliser B₂), ω₁+½ω₄+½ω₆+ω₈; A₆ (centraliser 2A₁), ½ω₁+½ω₄+½ω₇+½ω₈; A₄+A₂ (centraliser 2A₁), ½ω₁+½ω₅+½ω₈; A₂+2A₁ (centraliser B₃+A₁), ½ω₂+½ω₈ (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 8.5(3)–(5)); there are none for G₂ and E₆ in this sector. Without the restriction on s_c the list is not exhaustive: the G₂ witness (SRU.5 g2-noncentral-witness) gives a geometric unitary s ∈ CS(G₂, 0) with real part ½ω₂ ≠ 0 (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E18).
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
G of connected centre
s = s_c q^ν with s_c = 1 or s_c central in G^∨.
proofSteps: As in extraneous-classical, ν ∈ CS(G(O^∨), 0)₀ is, on each simple factor of z(O^∨), 0 or an exception of Theorem 6.14; the exceptional orbits and centraliser types come from the tables of nilpotent orbits (gaps: nilpotent-orbit owner pending).

For each remaining candidate compute the simple-root and fundamental-weight pairings of G^∨; the survivors are those listed (Ciubotaru–Harris, proof of Theorem 8.5, case (4)); the F₄, B₃ coordinate is corrected by comparison with Ciubotaru's F₄ classification (E5).
acceptance: For F₄ and O^∨ = B₃ the corrected point ω₁ + ½ω₃ + ½ω₄ has Euclidean coordinates (5/2, 1, ½, 0) in (6.21), Weyl-conjugate to the B₃ complementary-series parameter at ν = ½.
For G₂ the restricted sector has no extraneous point, while the noncentral witness s_c s_{½ω₂} is extraneous.

nodes.title: The extra E₈, 4A₁ region has no half-integral points
nodes.statement: For G of type E₈ and O^∨ = 4A₁ (Z(O^∨) of type C₄), in the coordinates ℜ(s) = ½h^∨ + (0, 0, ν₁, ν₁, ν₂, ν₂, −ν₃ + ν₄, ν₃ + ν₄) with 0 ≤ ν₁ ≤ ν₂ ≤ ν₃ ≤ ν₄, the complementary series is {ν₄ < ½} ∪ {ν₁ + ν₄ < 1, ν₂ + ν₃ < 1, ν₂ + ν₄ > 1, −ν₁ + ν₃ + ν₄ < 3/2 < ν₁ + ν₃ + ν₄} ((8.8)), and its extra region (the second set) contains no parameter half-integral for the adjoint representation (Ciubotaru–Harris §8.3; the case labels are corrected in PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26/E14).
hypotheses: G of type E₈; coordinates of Barbasch–Ciubotaru Table 13 and §6.4.1 as used by Ciubotaru–Harris.
proofSteps: Adjoint half-integrality forces all νᵢ ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0} or all in ¼ + ½ℤ (the second case is empty in these coordinates, E14).
In the first case ν₁ + ν₄ < 1 and ν₂ + ν₄ > 1 are incompatible with νᵢ ∈ ½ℤ; in the second, ν₄ = ¾ forces ν₂ = ν₃ = ¾, contradicting ν₂ + ν₃ < 1.
The region {ν₄ < ½} is CS(C₄, 0) and is handled by extraneous-exceptional as for other orbits.

The two E₈ lattice cases are checked separately: half-integer coordinates and ν₄<1 give ν₄≤½, contradicting ν₂+ν₄>1; quarter-integer coordinates give ν₄=¾ and ν₂>¼, hence ν₂≥¾ and ν₂+ν₃≥3/2, contradicting ν₂+ν₃<1. This also fixes the switched case labels in CH26 §8.3; the suggested Lean inequalities express these same two cases.
acceptance: The point ν = (½, ½, ½, ½) violates ν₁ + ν₄ < 1; the point (¼, ¾, ¾, ¾) violates ν₂ + ν₃ < 1.

sources.match: For 4A₁ in E₈ the complementary series has an extra region beyond CS(C₄, 0); a finite case analysis shows it has no adjoint-half-integral parameter (with the case labels corrected, E14).

nodes.title: Unitarity with noncentral compact part reduces to the centraliser of s_c
nodes.statement: Let k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting). For s = s_c q^ν with s_c compact (noncentral allowed) and ν real, L(s) is unitarizable iff the spherical module of the graded affine Hecke algebra attached to the centraliser Z_{G^∨}(s_c) (its root datum and the Hecke parameters determined by s_c) at the real parameter ν is unitary (Barbasch–Moy 1993). Unitarity of L(s) is therefore not governed by U₀^g of G when s_c is noncentral; the generic temperedness test and the extraneous-point lists of SRU.5 and SRU.7 are stated only for real or central-compact s.
hypotheses: k a nonarchimedean local field (any characteristic) with residue field 𝔽_q, G = 𝐆(k) with 𝐆 quasi-simple and split, I ⊂ K = 𝐆(O) an Iwahori subgroup, G^∨ the complex dual group with Lie algebra g^∨ (Ciubotaru–Harris §8 setting).
s_c compact, possibly noncentral.
proofSteps: Lusztig's reduction identifies the completion of H(G, I) at the central character of s with that of the graded Hecke algebra of Z_{G^∨}(s_c); Barbasch–Moy make it compatible with the *-structures (SRU.5 barbasch-moy-unitarity, third clause).
The G₂ witness shows the dependence: Z_{G₂}(s_c) has type A₁ × Ã₁, in whose graded algebra ½ω₂ lies in the complementary series, although it is not in U₀^g(G₂).
acceptance: For s_c central, Z_{G^∨}(s_c) = G^∨ and the statement reduces to SRU.5.
For G₂ and the involution s_c of g2-noncentral-witness, the centraliser is of type A₁ × Ã₁.

sources.match: By [BM2] the unitarity problem reduces to graded Hecke algebras of a possibly smaller group at real infinitesimal character.

restructure.detail:
The paper extractions propose Part II continuations of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups in nine independent directions: the unitary dual and the unitary spherical dual (Gan–Savin Appendix B, Gan–Ichino Appendix A, Ciubotaru–Harris §§4.2, 6–8), and the seven listed below. They share no definitions beyond the base roadmap: types and supercuspidal constructions, parahoric centres, unitary level-raising Hecke operators, characters and trace Paley–Wiener, mod p Bernstein centres, GL_n newforms and Newton cocentres each start from SR.0–SR.6 in a different direction, and together they exceed a thousand items. This packet plans the first listed direction, unitary spherical representations (Ciubotaru–Harris), together with the unitary dual (Gan–Savin), which its brief imports and which no other roadmap owns: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroupsPartII is the coalescence of the routes SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitaryDual and SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitarySpherical. The other directions:
- SmoothRepresentationsPartII ("Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations"): Fintzen 2021 (71 items), Stevens 2008 (280), Kurinczuk–Skodlerack–Stevens 2021 (369), Lust–Stevens 2020 (102), Bushnell–Henniart 2017 (78), Le–Le Hung–Levin–Morra 2023 (13), Newton–Thorne 2021 and 2021 II (6 + 1), Gan–Harris–Sawin et al. 2024 (3), Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor 2001 (2), Nakamura 2023 (1). Scope: Moy–Prasad filtrations at all depths, Yu's construction, types and Bushnell–Kutzko covers beyond the Iwahori and distinguished GL_n cases that SR.5.2 owns, semisimple characters and endo-parameters for classical groups, depth-zero L-packets, inertial types for GL₂ (Henniart); it imports SR.0–SR.3 and ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3. It is by far the largest direction (about 930 items) and is itself a candidate for a further split into a general-group branch (Fintzen, Yu) and a classical-group branch (Stevens, Kurinczuk–Skodlerack–Stevens, Lust–Stevens).
- SmoothRepresentationsPartIIParahoricCenters ("Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: parahoric centers"): Kisin–Pappas 2018 (3), He 2021 (10), Zhu 2017 (3), Clozel–Thorne 2017 (2), Dor 2023 (2), Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne 2019 (1). Scope: centres of parahoric Hecke algebras via the Iwahori centre and normalised e_P (Haines), change of parahoric, Bernstein functions; imports SR.1 and SR.4 (Iwahori–Matsumoto, Bernstein presentation and centre) and ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4.
- UnitaryLevelRaisingTypesAndHeckeOperators ("Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: unitary level-raising types and Hecke operators"): Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu 2022 (49). Scope: types and Hecke operators for unramified unitary groups U_N and the non-quasi-split U'_{2r} with special maximal level, used for level raising; imports SR.4.4 (unramified unitary groups).
- SmoothRepresentationsCharactersPartII ("Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: characters, trace Paley–Wiener and ℓ-adic lattices"): Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein 2022 (15), Hansen 2026 (9). Scope: Kazhdan's density theorem, the trace Paley–Wiener theorem, constant terms and the Bernstein–Deligne–Kazhdan restriction, Harish-Chandra characters beyond ET.4, ℓ-adic lattices in smooth representations; it should import this roadmap's SRU.3 character-weak-convergence and characters-linearly-independent rather than restate them.
- ModPBernsteinCentersAndLocalBaseChange ("Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: mod p Bernstein centers, the Brauer homomorphism and local cyclic base change"): Feng 2024 (32), Gan–Harris–Sawin et al. 2024 (1). Scope: mod p Hecke algebras at Moy–Prasad level, the base-change homomorphism of Bernstein centres via the Brauer homomorphism (Treumann–Venkatesh), local cyclic base change for Genestier–Lafforgue parameters; imports SR.6 and ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction.
- SmoothRepresentationsPartIIGeneralLinearNewforms ("Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: general-linear newforms"): Atobe–Kondo–Yasuda 2022 (59). Scope: local newforms for GL_n over a non-archimedean field; the design must first check AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2 (generic finite-place newforms) and QuiverRepresentationsPartII (multisegment duality, from the same paper), which already own parts of it.
- SmoothRepresentationsPartIINewtonCocenters ("Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: Newton cocenters and invariant distributions"): He 2018 (52). Scope: the Newton decomposition of the cocentre of the Hecke algebra, rigid cocentres, and invariant distributions; imports SR.1.
restructure.proposal: Split. Keep SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroupsPartII as "Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: unitary representations, the Fell topology and the unitary spherical dual" with stages SRU.0–SRU.7 as planned here, absorbing the route ids SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitaryDual and SmoothRepresentationsPartIIUnitarySpherical (their consumers, LocalLanglandsCorrespondenceForG2 and the routes MetaplecticAutomorphicFormsPartIIShimuraWaldspurger and GlobalShtukasPartIIRamanujanArthur of the pending Part II designs of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands, import its stages). Give each of the seven other route ids a design job of its own, as roadmaps with parent SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, each starting where SR stops in its direction and importing this roadmap where it touches unitarity (SmoothRepresentationsCharactersPartII: SRU.3 characters; SmoothRepresentationsPartII: SRU.4 isolation of supercuspidals). Boundaries: this roadmap owns unitary structures, unitary representations of locally compact groups, weak containment and the Fell topology, the Gan–Savin limit and isolation theorems, the generic unitary spherical dual of split and unramified groups, the Aubert–Zelevinsky involution for general reductive groups and the Kazhdan–Lusztig organisation of the spherical complementary series; it does not own types, Moy–Prasad theory beyond what RG2.3 states, parahoric centres, Kazhdan density or trace Paley–Wiener.

sourceIssues.locator: Forum Math. Pi 11 (2023) e28, §11.1, proof of Proposition 11.3, p. 32 (the definition of f_τ before Lemma 11.4); same text in arXiv:2209.07346v2
sourceIssues.printed: f_τ is defined on K as the complex conjugate of the character of τ divided by vol(K), and π(f_τ) is said to be the projector onto the τ-isotypic subspace.
sourceIssues.correction: f_τ = (dim τ / vol K) · conj χ_τ on K; without the factor dim τ, π(f_τ) is 1/dim τ times the isotypic projector.
sourceIssues.reason: For compact K with normalised Haar measure the isotypic projector is dim τ · ∫_K conj χ_τ(k) π(k) dk (Schur orthogonality); for K finite acting on ℂ[K] and τ of dimension 2 the printed operator has eigenvalue 1/2 on the τ-isotypic part. Lemma 11.4 only needs ⟨π(f_τ)v, v⟩ ≠ 0, so the argument is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:2311.15300v1, §6, the sentence after Definition 6.3 and (6.1), p. 17
sourceIssues.printed: With χ_s = s ∘ val_T as in (6.1) and s_ν = exp(ν log q), the text says that for dominant ν the spherical L(ν) is the unique irreducible quotient of X(ν).
sourceIssues.correction: With (6.1), for dominant ν the spherical L(ν) is the unique irreducible subrepresentation of X(ν) (equivalently the unique quotient of X(−ν)); the quotient statement holds in Barbasch–Ciubotaru's convention χ_ν(τ(a)) = |a|^{⟨τ,ν⟩}, which is opposite in sign.
sourceIssues.reason: By (6.1), val_T(λ^∨(ϖ)) = λ^∨, so χ_{s_ν}(λ^∨(ϖ)) = q^{⟨λ^∨, ν⟩}. For PGL₂ and ν = ρ this gives χ = δ_B^{−1/2}, and i_B(δ_B^{−1/2}) = Ind_B^G 1 contains the trivial representation L(ρ) as a subrepresentation, not as a quotient. No subsequent step uses the quotient statement except through unitarity, which is unchanged under ν ↦ −ν.
